summary: Research the 4 open AEGIS design questions: options/combo strategy taxonomy, TP/SL strategies (tranche/trailing/greeks), 2-level multi-leg model, clean-window equity heuristic (Sonnet, academic-first)
logs: aegis-strategy-research: 4 parallel academic-first research streams -> synthesis

single_leg.name: Long Call
single_leg.risk_profile: Defined risk. Max loss = premium paid. Max gain = unlimited (underlying - strike - premium). Net positive delta, positive vega, negative theta.
single_leg.when_used: HIGH conviction bullish view; low-IV regime (cheap extrinsic — paying less for optionality). Capital-efficient substitute for stock. Avoids defined-risk cap of debit spread when large move expected.

single_leg.name: Long Put
single_leg.risk_profile: Defined risk. Max loss = premium paid. Max gain = strike - premium (underlying can go to zero). Net negative delta, positive vega, negative theta.
single_leg.when_used: HIGH conviction bearish thesis OR portfolio hedge in low-IV regime (relatively cheap protection). Avoid in HIGH-IV regime — paying inflated premium.

single_leg.name: Short Call (naked)
single_leg.risk_profile: UNDEFINED risk. Max gain = premium received. Max loss = unlimited (theoretical). Net negative delta, negative vega, positive theta.
single_leg.when_used: REJECTED under no-naked-leverage posture. Requires margin that cannot be represented as collateral-secured under the ADR-0027 O2 rule. Never admissible in AEGIS unless paired with a covering position (becomes covered call or bear call spread).

single_leg.name: Short Put (naked / cash-secured)
single_leg.risk_profile: Collateral-secured variant (CSP): defined risk = strike × 100 × contracts (assignment exposure), premium offsets. Naked variant: undefined risk — REJECTED. Net positive delta, negative vega, positive theta.
single_leg.when_used: HIGH-IV regime; bullish or neutral stance. CSP: get paid to potentially buy stock at a discount. Entry: IV-rank >= 50 (HIGH regime), 30-45 DTE, 0.20–0.30 delta strike, sufficient cash collateral (strike × 100 × contracts in buying power). Academic: CBOE PUT index (put-write strategy) outperformed BXM on risk-adjusted basis in multiple studies (Whaley 2002, Black & Szado 2022 family). ONLY the cash-secured variant is admissible in AEGIS.

single_leg.name: Covered Call (CC)
single_leg.legs: LONG 100 shares + SELL 1 OTM call (0.20–0.30 delta, 30–45 DTE)
single_leg.risk_profile: Collateral-secured. Max gain = (strike - cost basis) × 100 + premium. Max loss = (cost basis - premium) × 100 (stock goes to zero). Net delta = 100 - (delta × 100) ≈ 70–80 shares equivalent.
single_leg.when_used: HIGH IV-regime; bearish lean on near-term move, existing long stock position. The BXM index (CBOE S&P 500 BuyWrite, ticker BXM) is the canonical benchmark: systematically sells 1-month ATM calls. Academic: Whaley 2002, Hill et al. 2006 (Financial Analysts Journal) — BXM produced lower Sharpe on standard basis but competitive on drawdown-adjusted, especially in range-bound/down markets. Worst in strong bull runs (capped upside). Wysocki & Slepaczuk 2024 (arXiv 2407.13908): OTM short call with VIX-based sizing produced best stable risk-adjusted results (6.5% aRC, low drawdown), 2018–2023 SPX backtest.

multi_leg_options.name: Bull Call Spread (debit vertical)
multi_leg_options.legs: BUY 1 call at lower strike + SELL 1 call at higher strike, same expiry (both OTM or ATM/OTM)
multi_leg_options.risk_profile: Defined risk. Max loss = net debit paid. Max gain = (spread width - net debit) × 100. Net positive delta, near-zero vega (less sensitive to IV than long call), negative theta.
multi_leg_options.when_used: Moderate bullish view; any IV regime (debit spreads are less sensitive to IV than naked longs). Preferred in HIGH-IV regime over long call (reduces vega exposure while defining risk). Capital-efficient: lower premium than outright long call. Capped upside — only suitable when price target is within the spread width.

multi_leg_options.name: Bear Put Spread (debit vertical)
multi_leg_options.legs: BUY 1 put at higher strike + SELL 1 put at lower strike, same expiry
multi_leg_options.risk_profile: Defined risk. Max loss = net debit. Max gain = (spread width - net debit) × 100. Net negative delta, near-zero vega, negative theta.
multi_leg_options.when_used: Moderate bearish view; HIGH-IV regime (reduces vega vs. long put). Defined risk hedge or directional play. Academic: McKeon 2016 (Journal of Asset Management) showed directional vertical spreads generate returns correlated with underlying direction.

multi_leg_options.name: Bull Put Spread (credit vertical / put credit spread)
multi_leg_options.legs: SELL 1 OTM put at higher strike + BUY 1 put at lower strike (protection), same expiry
multi_leg_options.risk_profile: Defined risk. Max gain = net credit received. Max loss = (spread width - net credit) × 100. Net positive delta, negative vega, positive theta.
multi_leg_options.when_used: HIGH-IV regime; bullish or neutral thesis. Collects premium with defined downside. Superior to naked CSP in capital efficiency — same directional thesis, defined max loss. Iron condor is two of these stacked. Chaput & Ederington 2003 (Journal of Derivatives): vertical spread design is the most common institutional income structure.

multi_leg_options.name: Bear Call Spread (credit vertical / call credit spread)
multi_leg_options.legs: SELL 1 OTM call at lower strike + BUY 1 call at higher strike (protection), same expiry
multi_leg_options.risk_profile: Defined risk. Max gain = net credit. Max loss = (spread width - net credit) × 100. Net negative delta, negative vega, positive theta.
multi_leg_options.when_used: HIGH-IV regime; bearish or neutral view. Often the upper wing of an iron condor. In isolation: take income when expected range ceiling is the short strike.

multi_leg_options.name: Iron Condor (short)
multi_leg_options.legs: SELL OTM put + BUY further OTM put (bull put spread) + SELL OTM call + BUY further OTM call (bear call spread); same expiry, 4 strikes
multi_leg_options.risk_profile: Defined risk. Max gain = total net credit (both spreads). Max loss = wider wing width × 100 - net credit. Profit zone = between two short strikes. Negative vega, positive theta, near-zero net delta (if symmetric). Niblock 2017 (Applied Finance Letters): short-volatility condors outperformed long-volatility condors on risk-adjusted basis; best in falling/stable IV. CBOE has CNDR index.
multi_leg_options.when_used: HIGH IV-regime; neutral / range-bound thesis; expecting IV contraction. Key selling point per Wikipedia/CBOE: same margin requirement as a single vertical spread but two premium credits. 30–45 DTE, short strikes at 0.15–0.20 delta each side. Classic theta-capture: profit if underlying stays in range and IV falls. Wysocki & Slepaczuk 2024: 5% OTM short strangle (the no-wing version) with delta sizing IR*** = 64.16 — strongest pure risk-adjusted result in their SPX study.

multi_leg_options.name: Iron Butterfly (short iron butterfly / short ironfly)
multi_leg_options.legs: SELL 1 ATM call + SELL 1 ATM put (same strike, ATM body) + BUY 1 OTM call wing + BUY 1 OTM put wing; same expiry
multi_leg_options.risk_profile: Defined risk. Max gain = net credit (when underlying pins exactly at body strike). Max loss = wing width × 100 - net credit. Negative vega, positive theta, near-zero net delta at inception. Narrower profit zone but higher credit than iron condor for same wing width. CBOE has BFLY index.
multi_leg_options.when_used: HIGH IV-regime; very strong neutral conviction with pin expectation. Used when trader expects very little movement — tighter than iron condor. Academic: iron butterfly vs. condor — butterfly provides higher premium but narrower profit zone; condor provides wider zone but lower credit. Wysocki & Slepaczuk 2024: ATM short straddle (bodyless equivalent) showed −1.2% to +4.9% aRC depending on sizing; the wider strike wing version (short strangle) was superior.

multi_leg_options.name: Long Straddle
multi_leg_options.legs: BUY 1 ATM call + BUY 1 ATM put, same strike and expiry
multi_leg_options.directional_bias: Neutral (long volatility — profits from large moves in either direction)
multi_leg_options.risk_profile: Defined risk. Max loss = total premium paid (if underlying pins at strike). Max gain = unlimited (upside on call side) / strike - total premium (downside on put side). Positive vega, negative theta.
multi_leg_options.when_used: LOW IV-regime; expectation of large move but uncertain direction (earnings, binary events). Expires worthless if underlying stays near strike — theta bleeds premium. Academic: Wysocki & Slepaczuk 2024 showed short straddles produced modest positive returns with VIX sizing (3.0% aRC, IR 1.77) over 2018–2023; the long version was implicitly worse given the selling edge in the volatility risk premium (VRP).

multi_leg_options.name: Long Strangle
multi_leg_options.legs: BUY 1 OTM put + BUY 1 OTM call, different strikes (typically 0.20–0.30 delta), same expiry
multi_leg_options.risk_profile: Defined risk. Max loss = total premium paid. Max gain = large (unlimited upside through call, stock-to-zero through put). Lower premium than straddle; wider breakeven range required. Positive vega, negative theta.
multi_leg_options.when_used: LOW IV-regime; expectation of very large move but uncertain direction. Cheaper than straddle; needs a larger underlying move to profit. Academic: Wysocki & Slepaczuk 2024 — the SHORT strangle outperformed most strategies at 5% OTM (10.3% aRC, IR*** 64.2); therefore the LONG strangle is the losing side of that edge — only appropriate near earnings or binary catalyst.

multi_leg_options.name: Short Straddle
multi_leg_options.legs: SELL 1 ATM call + SELL 1 ATM put, same strike and expiry
multi_leg_options.risk_profile: UNDEFINED risk (naked legs). Max gain = total premium received. Max loss = unlimited (both sides). Negative vega, positive theta. REJECTED under no-naked-leverage posture — both legs are naked unless separately collateralized.
multi_leg_options.when_used: REJECTED in AEGIS (undefined risk; both short legs are naked — no collateral can simultaneously cover both a short call and a short put on the same underlying). Must be converted to iron butterfly if this thesis is expressed.

multi_leg_options.name: Short Strangle
multi_leg_options.legs: SELL 1 OTM call + SELL 1 OTM put, same expiry but different strikes (both OTM)
multi_leg_options.risk_profile: UNDEFINED risk (both legs naked). Max gain = total premium received. Max loss = unlimited. REJECTED under no-naked-leverage posture — same naked-short objection as short straddle.
multi_leg_options.when_used: REJECTED in AEGIS as naked. If this thesis is desired, it must be expressed as an iron condor (add wings to define risk). Wysocki & Slepaczuk 2024 found the 5% OTM short strangle had the highest IR*** (64.2) among all strategies tested — which means this is the HIGHEST-PRIORITY strategy to express via its defined-risk wrapper (iron condor) once multi-leg producer extension is complete.

multi_leg_options.name: Calendar Spread (time spread / horizontal spread)
multi_leg_options.legs: SELL 1 near-term option (shorter DTE) + BUY 1 same-strike option (longer DTE), same underlying and type (both calls or both puts)
multi_leg_options.directional_bias: Neutral to mildly directional (depends on strike vs. spot)
multi_leg_options.risk_profile: Defined risk. Max loss = net debit paid. Max gain = roughly the difference in extrinsic value between legs (difficult to compute precisely; model-dependent). Positive vega (long the longer-dated leg), positive theta if near-term decay exceeds long-leg decay. Profits from time decay differential and/or IV increase.
multi_leg_options.when_used: LOW-MID IV-regime; neutral view; expecting IV expansion. The near-term leg decays faster; if IV rises, the long back leg appreciates more. ADR-0029 Open Question 1: Alpaca paper calendar spread support (different-expiry legs) not yet verified. Deferred until broker probe confirms multi-expiry mleg support.

multi_leg_options.name: Diagonal Spread (PMCC base structure)
multi_leg_options.legs: BUY 1 deep-ITM long-dated option (LEAPS, 0.70–0.90 delta, 365–730 DTE) + SELL 1 near-term OTM option (0.20–0.30 delta, 30–45 DTE), same type (calls for bullish diagonal); different strikes AND different expirations
multi_leg_options.directional_bias: Directional (call diagonal = bullish; put diagonal = bearish)
multi_leg_options.risk_profile: Defined risk. Max loss = net debit (if underlying collapses below long strike). Max gain = (short strike - long strike) × 100 + premium credits accumulated from rolling. Net positive delta (call diagonal), positive theta from rolling, initially positive vega (long the LEAPS).
multi_leg_options.when_used: ANY IV-regime for the LEAPS purchase; HIGH-IV preferred for the short near-term leg (maximizes rolling credits). The PMCC shadow tracker in hermes-quant (docs/design/pmcc-shadow-tracker.md) is seeded with AMZN LEAPS Dec-2027 $205C + short Jul-2026 $285C: net debit $8,202 vs $27,064 for 100 shares (32% capital), net theta +$9.95/day. Capital-efficient covered-call substitute — primary value is the same premium-capture thesis at ~30% of share capital.

multi_leg_options.name: Long Butterfly (call butterfly or put butterfly)
multi_leg_options.legs: BUY 1 lower-strike option + SELL 2 middle-strike options + BUY 1 higher-strike option, all same type and expiry (equal wing width)
multi_leg_options.risk_profile: Defined risk. Net debit (typically small). Max gain = wing width - net debit (if underlying pins at middle strike). Max loss = net debit. Very low cost, very high risk-adjusted max return but narrow profit zone.
multi_leg_options.when_used: HIGH-conviction neutral view expecting pin at a specific strike; ANY IV-regime (low cost means IV doesn't dominate). Often used as a precision target for earnings. Academic: CBOE BFLY index tracks this systematically on S&P 500.

multi_leg_options.name: Ratio Spread (call ratio or put ratio)
multi_leg_options.legs: BUY 1 option at near strike + SELL 2 (or more) options at further strike, same type and expiry (e.g., 1x2 ratio call spread: BUY 1 ATM call, SELL 2 OTM calls)
multi_leg_options.risk_profile: PARTIALLY UNDEFINED risk. The extra short leg(s) beyond the long leg's coverage are naked. Max gain = between the two strikes. Max loss = unlimited (upside for call ratio; downside for put ratio) on the unhedged short legs. Chaput & Ederington 2008 (Journal of Derivatives) documented ratio spread design as a practitioner structure.
multi_leg_options.when_used: REJECTED in AEGIS for the naked-short portion. The 1-leg-long / 1-leg-short variant with equal quantities is a vertical spread (admissible); any >1 short-per-long ratio creates naked exposure. If ratio spread thesis is desired, cap the short legs at the long leg count — converts to vertical spread.

multi_leg_options.name: Back Spread (reverse ratio spread)
multi_leg_options.legs: SELL 1 option at near strike + BUY 2 (or more) options at further OTM strike, same type and expiry (e.g., call back spread: SELL 1 ATM call, BUY 2 OTM calls)
multi_leg_options.risk_profile: Defined risk on the long side (loss capped at strike width - credit). Loss zone is between the two strikes; unlimited gain beyond the further strike. Positive vega, complex theta.
multi_leg_options.when_used: LOW IV-regime (buying cheap OTM options for large-move convexity). Rare in systematic income-oriented books. Defined risk on the debit side but complex loss zone. Permissible if max loss is computed and gated (the selling side is covered by the buying side structurally — it's a debit spread variant with extra longs).

multi_leg_options.name: Box Spread
multi_leg_options.legs: LONG call spread (bull call) + LONG put spread (bear put) at same strikes and expiry: BUY call at K1, SELL call at K2, BUY put at K2, SELL put at K1 (all same expiry). Results in riskless payoff = (K2 - K1) × 100 regardless of underlying.
multi_leg_options.risk_profile: Effectively zero market risk. Used as a financing mechanism (borrowing/lending at the options-implied rate). Profit/loss = difference between spread width and net premium paid/received minus financing cost.
multi_leg_options.when_used: NOT a directional or income strategy. Used by institutions for balance-sheet financing. Not relevant to a systematic equity book with directional or income thesis. EXCLUDED from AEGIS strategy universe — no market thesis, and the capital tie-up versus actual financing cost is better expressed via cash or T-bills.

stock_option_combos.name: Covered Call (CC)
stock_option_combos.legs: LONG 100 shares underlying + SELL 1 OTM call (0.20–0.30 delta, 30–45 DTE). The CC is simultaneously a single-leg category AND a stock+option combo — listed in both for completeness.
stock_option_combos.risk_profile: Collateral-secured. Max gain = (call strike - stock cost basis + premium) × 100. Max loss = (cost basis - premium received) × 100 (stock goes to zero). Net delta ≈ 70–80 per 100 shares (stock delta minus short call delta). Positive theta from short call, lower vega than pure stock position. CBOE BXM index (ATM monthly CC on S&P 500): historically lower Sharpe than buy-and-hold but competitive drawdown-adjusted in flat/down markets (Whaley 2002; Black & Szado 2022 family; Wysocki & Slepaczuk 2024 — OTM CC outperformed ATM CC).
stock_option_combos.when_used: HIGH IV-regime; existing stock position; neutral-to-bearish near-term view but long-term bullish thesis. Gate: held_shares >= 100 × contracts (ADR-0027 O2 collateral check). Current AEGIS producer can build this.

stock_option_combos.name: Cash-Secured Put (CSP)
stock_option_combos.legs: HOLD cash equal to strike × 100 × contracts + SELL 1 OTM put (0.20–0.30 delta, 30–45 DTE)
stock_option_combos.risk_profile: Collateral-secured. Max gain = premium received. Max loss = (strike - premium) × 100 × contracts (assignment exposure offset by premium). Net positive delta, negative vega, positive theta. CBOE PUT index (systematic CSP on S&P 500): outperformed BXM on Sharpe in several academic studies (Black & Szado; multiple CBOE whitepapers). Wysocki & Slepaczuk 2024: ATM short put with VIX sizing showed 6.6% aRC, IR*** 20.3 — best single-leg income result in their study.
stock_option_combos.when_used: HIGH IV-regime; bullish or neutral stance; willing to own the underlying at the strike price. Gate: options_buying_power >= strike × 100 × contracts - premium (ADR-0027 three-bucket CSP check). Current AEGIS producer can build this. The SHORT-leg-first income strategy most directly supported by put-write index evidence.

stock_option_combos.name: Wheel (CC-to-CSP cycle)
stock_option_combos.legs: State machine: START with CSP -> if assigned (stock purchased): transition to CC -> if called away (stock sold): return to CSP. Both legs collateral-secured at every state.
stock_option_combos.directional_bias: Neutral to bullish on the underlying (wheels only make sense on names you are willing to own)
stock_option_combos.risk_profile: Collateral-secured at all times (cash during CSP phase; shares during CC phase). Max loss = (assignment price - combined premium credits) × 100 if stock declines sharply in CSP phase. Continuous theta collection. The combined income stream can reduce effective cost basis over multiple cycles.
stock_option_combos.when_used: HIGH IV-regime; neutral-to-bullish underlying thesis; capital-efficient income generation on a single name. Gate: composite_intent='wheel' budgets collateral ONCE (ADR-0027 D7 amendment) — the CSP collateral and CC share collateral are not double-counted. Current AEGIS producer (structure_select.py) maps NEUTRAL + PREMIUM_CAPTURE + MID/HIGH IV -> wheel. Academic: no direct wheel-strategy benchmark index; typically analyzed as the sum of its CSP and CC legs.

stock_option_combos.name: Protective Put (married put)
stock_option_combos.legs: LONG 100 shares + BUY 1 OTM put (protective; typically 0.20–0.30 delta, 60–90 DTE)
stock_option_combos.risk_profile: Defined risk with premium cost. Max loss = (stock price - put strike) × 100 + premium paid (floored at put strike). Max gain = unlimited (uncapped upside from stock + put worth zero at expiry). Cost = premium drag on returns. Net delta = stock delta - put delta ≈ 70–80 (reduces directional exposure). Positive vega.
stock_option_combos.when_used: LOW-to-MID IV-regime (cheap puts for protection); HIGH-conviction bullish position that needs tail protection (regulatory event, earnings). A collar removes the premium drag at the cost of capped upside. Academic: protective puts as portfolio insurance — Bookstaber & Clarke 1984 (Journal of Business) foundational; Benninga & Blume 1985 on portfolio insurance optimality.

stock_option_combos.name: Collar
stock_option_combos.legs: LONG 100 shares + BUY 1 OTM put (downside protection, 0.20–0.30 delta) + SELL 1 OTM call (upside cap, 0.20–0.30 delta), same expiry
stock_option_combos.risk_profile: Defined risk (both-sided). Max loss = (stock price - put strike - net premium) × 100. Max gain = (call strike - stock price + net premium) × 100. The short call premium partially or fully finances the long put. Zero-cost collar: net premium ≈ 0 (put premium = call premium). Net delta ≈ 50–70 (stock partially hedged both ways).
stock_option_combos.when_used: When protecting a large unrealized gain on a long stock position while retaining upside to a target price. HIGH-conviction on holding the stock long-term but near-term uncertainty. Zero-cost collar minimizes premium drag. Academic: collar-finance-wikipedia; widely used by institutional holders for hedging concentrated positions.

stock_option_combos.name: PMCC — Poor Man's Covered Call (long diagonal)
stock_option_combos.legs: BUY 1 deep-ITM LEAPS call (0.70–0.90 delta, 365–730 DTE) + SELL 1 near-term OTM call (0.20–0.30 delta, 30–45 DTE), same underlying
stock_option_combos.directional_bias: Bullish (long delta via LEAPS, income from short call)
stock_option_combos.risk_profile: Defined risk. Max loss = net debit (LEAPS cost - accumulated short call credits). Risk condition: short strike must be above LEAPS strike or assignment creates a debit spread loss scenario. Max gain per cycle = short strike - LEAPS strike + rolling credits. Net positive delta ≈ 35–60, net positive theta (rolling credits exceed LEAPS decay when managed well), initially positive vega. hermes-quant shadow tracker: AMZN PMCC net theta +$9.95/day, net debit $8,202 vs $27,064 for 100 shares (32% of share capital).
stock_option_combos.when_used: Bullish thesis; HIGH IV-regime (maximize short call credit); stock too expensive for 100 shares but want CC-equivalent economics. Capital-efficient: ~30–40% of the capital of the equivalent covered call. Rolling the short leg monthly provides ongoing income. Requires careful management: net debit must be recoverable through rolling credits.

stock_option_combos.name: Covered Strangle
stock_option_combos.legs: LONG 100 shares + SELL 1 OTM call (0.20–0.30 delta) + SELL 1 OTM put (0.20–0.30 delta), same expiry
stock_option_combos.risk_profile: The call is covered by 100 shares. The put is cash-secured (not naked). Max gain = call premium + put premium if stock stays between strikes. Max loss = (stock falls far below put strike) × 100 - total premium received + (put strike - stock) × 100. Net delta ≈ 100 - short call delta + short put delta. Higher total premium than CC alone. PARTIALLY UNDEFINED risk if the put is not cash-secured.
stock_option_combos.when_used: HIGH IV-regime; neutral/flat view on the underlying. Only admissible if: (a) call is covered by 100 shares AND (b) the put is cash-secured. Gate must check BOTH legs independently. Reject if the put would be naked. Both the CC and CSP components must pass the three-bucket classifier independently.

stock_option_combos.name: Stock Replacement (synthetic long via deep-ITM call)
stock_option_combos.legs: BUY 1 deep-ITM call (0.80–0.95 delta, 90–180 DTE) as a proxy for 100 shares
stock_option_combos.risk_profile: Defined risk. Max loss = premium paid (vs. full stock loss for actual shares). Near-1.0 delta behavior. Higher time-value cost than direct stock ownership but dramatically lower capital deployment. Positive vega. Often used with rolling.
stock_option_combos.when_used: When thesis requires stock-like exposure but capital is constrained (e.g., deploying 5–10% NAV equivalent exposure at 30–40% of the actual equity capital). The deep-ITM call behaves like stock within normal move ranges. LOW-MID IV-regime preferred (minimizes extrinsic value paid). Often paired with a near-term OTM short call to form a PMCC.

taxonomy.risk_classification:
RISK CLASSIFICATION AND AEGIS ADMISSIBILITY

--- GROUP 1: DEFINED RISK (all upside/downside caps are finite at entry) ---
Admissible under no-naked-leverage posture. ALL max_loss values are finite and deterministic at entry.

Long Call / Long Put: defined risk = premium paid. Admissible.
Long Straddle / Long Strangle: defined risk = total premium paid. Admissible.
Bull Call Spread (debit vertical): defined risk = net debit. Admissible.
Bear Put Spread (debit vertical): defined risk = net debit. Admissible.
Bull Put Spread (credit vertical): defined risk = (spread width - credit) × 100. Admissible.
Bear Call Spread (credit vertical): defined risk = (spread width - credit) × 100. Admissible.
Iron Condor (long/short): defined risk = max wing width × 100 - net credit/debit. Admissible.
Iron Butterfly (long/short): defined risk = wing width × 100 - net credit. Admissible.
Long Butterfly: defined risk = small net debit. Admissible.
Calendar Spread (debit): defined risk = net debit (can be imprecise in theory). Admissible with caution.
Diagonal Spread / PMCC: defined risk = net debit. Admissible.
Long Back Spread: defined risk — the long legs exceed shorts; loss zone is bounded. Admissible if gated.
Protective Put / Married Put: defined risk = (stock cost - put strike) + premium. Admissible.
Collar: defined risk — both directions bounded. Admissible.
Stock Replacement (deep-ITM long call): defined risk = premium. Admissible.

--- GROUP 2: COLLATERAL-SECURED (undefined by formula, but risk is bounded by real assets held) ---
Admissible under no-naked-leverage posture PROVIDED the collateral check passes.

Covered Call (CC): short call covered by ≥100 shares. Admissible; ADR-0027 O2 checks held_shares >= 100 × contracts.
Cash-Secured Put (CSP): short put backed by options_buying_power ≥ strike × 100 × contracts - premium. Admissible.
Wheel: CSP + CC state machine. Admissible when each state independently clears its collateral check. ADR-0027 D7 composite_intent='wheel' budgets collateral ONCE.
PMCC (as collateral-secured variant): the long LEAPS call collateralizes the short near-term call, provided short strike ≥ long strike. Admissible.
Covered Strangle: call covered by shares + put cash-secured. Admissible if BOTH legs independently clear.

--- GROUP 3: UNDEFINED RISK (no upper/lower bound on loss at entry — REJECTED) ---
REJECTED under no-naked-leverage posture. These are the naked/uncovered structures that ADR-0027 O2 blocks.

Short Call (naked): unlimited upside loss. REJECTED.
Short Put (naked, not cash-secured): loss = strike × 100 × contracts. REJECTED (no collateral backing).
Short Straddle: both legs naked — REJECTED.
Short Strangle: both legs naked — REJECTED.
Ratio Spread (>1 short per long): the excess short legs are naked — REJECTED (the 1:1 vertical spread portion is admissible; only the excess is rejected).
Box Spread: not rejected for risk reasons (it is risk-free) but excluded from AEGIS strategy universe — it is a financing instrument not a directional/income strategy.

--- DISCRETE NAV-FRACTION LADDER MAPPING {0, ±0.05, ±0.10, ±0.15, ±0.20} ---

The ladder maps to CONTRACT COUNT via floor(target_nav_fraction × NAV / collateral_per_contract):

CC: collateral_per_contract = basis_per_share × 100 (the share value at entry). A 0.10 NAV step on a $100k book at $150/share = 1 contract (0.10 × 100,000 / 15,000 = 0.67 → floor = 0 for 5%; floor = 1 for 10%).
CSP: collateral_per_contract = strike × 100 (minus premium received). Same ladder math. At $150 strike: 0.10 × 100k / 15,000 = 0.67 → round down = 0 at 5% NAV step; 1 at 10% for a 100k book.
Vertical Spread / Iron Condor: collateral_per_contract = spread_width × 100 (the defined max loss). A $5-wide spread = $500 BPR per contract. 0.05 NAV = 10 contracts on a 100k book (0.05 × 100k / 500 = 10). Spreads are naturally MORE granular on the ladder than stock-backed structures.
PMCC: collateral_per_contract = net_debit (LEAPS cost minus accumulated credits). Generally similar to CSP.
Straddle/Strangle (long, admissible): collateral = total premium. Very small capital per contract; granular ladder.

Ladder discipline: the gate always FLOORS (never rounds up) and must verify contracts ≥ 1 (Rule 7 minimum guard). A target that maps to < 1 contract silences the proposal (same as a fractional-equity signal flooring to zero).

POSTURE SUMMARY: the no-naked-leverage constraint reduces the ~25 strategy variants to ~15 admissible structures. The key rejection class is any short leg that lacks a covering position (long option at a wider/same strike, long shares ≥ 100 per contract, or cash equal to the assignment value). tpsl.recommendation: Default approach for a thin-history systematic book: all-at-once hard stop + single all-at-once take-profit at the first ladder step that represents profit (e.g., close the full NAV-fraction position when P&L >= +1R target, stop the full position at the hard-stop level). This is the simplest, most auditable, and most testable design with no path-dependency; every parameter can be eval-gated independently. Escalate to tranche / trailing only after >= 60 sessions of paper data (and >= 30 round-trips) show a specific alpha edge that tranching or trailing would preserve. Escalate to greeks-based exits only after the options evidence window requirement (60 days / N >= 100 trades) is met.
methods: ALL-AT-ONCE: Close the full position at a single hard stop or single hard TP level. Pro: maximum simplicity, fully auditable, one parameter each, no path dependency. Con: forfeits potential upside if the trade keeps going and forces a binary hit-or-miss.

SCALE-OUT TRANCHES (R-multiple ladder): Exit fractions at successive R-multiples (e.g., 1/3 at +1R, 1/3 at +2R, trail the rest). Pro: banks partial profit early, reduces capital at risk, gives a trailing stop room to operate on a smaller residual without early liquidation of the whole position. Con: systematically lowers the average exit price on winners ('whipsaw' trades where price briefly touches +1R then reverses fully will still incur the partial TP while the remainder stops out), and introduces three parameters (tranche sizes + TP levels) that must all be eval-gated.

TRAILING STOP (fixed-% or breakeven-after-1R): Move stop up (long) / down (short) as price moves favorably; never move it adversely. Pro: asymmetric capture — lets winners run while containing losses. Con: whipsaw risk in mean-reverting or choppy regimes, noise-sensitive at tight widths, path-dependent complexity.

ATR-TRAILING (Chandelier exit): Trail at N x ATR(K) below recent high/above recent low. Pro: adapts trail width to realized volatility — widens during noisy markets to avoid premature exits, tightens during calm periods. Con: ATR is a lagging measure, must be sized large enough to avoid sub-noise triggers; requires a volatility baseline that a thin book may not yet have reliably.

GREEKS-BASED / DELTA-BREACH (options): Exit a short-premium structure when mark-to-market P&L >= 50% of max credit, or when short delta (absolute) breaches a threshold (e.g., short put that opened at delta 0.15 and now exceeds 0.40), or at 21 DTE when gamma acceleration overtakes theta income. Pro: exits driven by the economics of the position — theta captured vs. gamma risk remaining. Con: requires real-time greeks stream, delta signal is noisy near-the-money, 50% / 21 DTE heuristics are practitioner rules from tastylive internal research (not peer-reviewed), and the ATR-TP analog for options does not exist.

TIME-BASED (theta / DTE): Close options positions at a fixed DTE (e.g., 21 DTE) regardless of P&L, or close equity positions after N ticks if no target is hit ('stale close'). Pro: forces capital recycling, avoids gamma blowup near expiry for short premium. Con: exits winning positions prematurely if there is residual theta to collect, and exits losing positions that may have recovered; no evidence this outperforms P&L-triggered exits for equities.
tpsl.tranche_design:
CONCRETE TRANCHE SCALE-OUT DESIGN (equity positions on the discrete NAV-fraction ladder):

Ladder context: positions are whole-ladder increments {0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.20} of NAV. A tranche exit must move a position DOWN the ladder, not to an arbitrary fraction.

Example: Full position = 0.10 NAV (2 ladder steps of 0.05 each).
- Tranche 1 (1/2 of position): reduce from 0.10 to 0.05 when unrealized P&L >= +1R (where R = initial hard-stop distance in $NAV). Move hard stop to breakeven on remaining 0.05.
- Tranche 2 (residual): close the remaining 0.05 either (a) at hard TP +2R, OR (b) when trailing stop triggers (see trailing design).

RATIONALE FOR THIS DESIGN: The operator ask to 'leave room for trailing to not get liquidated early' is addressed by keeping the trailing stop on a SMALL residual (0.05 NAV) after Tranche 1 has been taken. A trailing stop on a 0.05 position can be set wider (in $ terms) without much capital at risk, so a noise-driven whipsaw on the residual is a small loss, not a large one. The trailing stop is never the sole risk-management mechanism for the full position.

FULL POSITION = 0.15 variant:
- At +1R: reduce to 0.10 (exit 1 step = 0.05).
- At +2R: reduce to 0.05 (exit another 0.05). Move stop to +1R on residual.
- Trail the 0.05 residual with chandelier ATR stop.

CONSTRAINT: Because the ladder is discrete, a 'tranche' is always a whole 0.05 step. Do NOT introduce fractional NAV positions just to enable a prettier tranche ratio (fractional positions violate the discreteness invariant).

STATUS: Both TP levels and the breakeven-step trigger are EVAL-GATE-PENDING (require walk-forward confirmation on our own data before production wiring).
tpsl.trailing_design:
CONCRETE TRAILING STOP DESIGN FOR AEGIS (30-min tick cadence, discrete ladder):

STEP 1 — Noise floor requirement: At 30-min bars, intraday ATR(14) for liquid equities runs roughly 0.3–1.2% per bar for mid-cap names. A trailing stop tighter than ~5% will be triggered by routine noise on most names. This matches the Li et al. 2026 finding that trailing distances of 2–3% (in the crypto context, analogous to even tighter for equities) combined with activation at 3% are the sweet spot. For equities at 30-min granularity, the minimum meaningful trailing distance is 5–7%.

STEP 2 — ATR-Chandelier design:
- Chandelier trailing stop (long): TRAIL = MAX(close over lookback K bars) - N x ATR(K)
- Chandelier trailing stop (short): TRAIL = MIN(close over lookback K bars) + N x ATR(K)
- Recommended starting point (EVAL-GATE-PENDING): K=14 bars (30-min), N=3.0 for a position with no prior tranche, N=2.0 for a residual tranche (already at half position, so tighter trail is acceptable).
- This means at a typical 1% per-bar ATR, the trail is 3% below the recent 14-bar high — comfortably above the 5% noise floor.

STEP 3 — Breakeven promotion rule (alternative simpler design):
- After price moves +1R above entry, move hard stop to ENTRY PRICE (breakeven). This is the 'breakeven-after-1R' variant.
- At +2R, move stop to +1R.
- This design is path-independent at each tick and requires only a running max-since-entry calculation; it does NOT require ATR.
- Tradeoff vs ATR-chandelier: breakeven-after-1R is regime-agnostic and cannot adapt to sudden volatility expansion; chandelier adapts but requires ATR history.

STEP 4 — Interaction with discrete ladder:
- The trailing stop NEVER promotes the position size UP the ladder. It only controls WHEN to close a rung.
- On a tick-by-tick basis (30-min cadence): at each bar close, compute the current chandelier level. If close crosses below (long) or above (short), execute the ladder reduction (close the affected tranche or full position at market open / next fill).
- Because AEGIS uses a 30-min cadence, the stop cannot fire intra-bar. This is actually safer: it avoids sub-5% intrabar noise hits.

STEP 5 — Concrete numbers (all EVAL-GATE-PENDING, never ground truth):
- Activation threshold: +3% unrealized P&L before trailing activates (prevents trailing on positions that haven't moved meaningfully; matching Li et al. 2026 top-5 result of 3% activation).
- Trailing distance: 5–7% for full position; 3–5% for residual half-position.
- ATR multiplier N: 2.5x ATR(14) as baseline. The Li et al. 2026 ATR overlay found 1.0x ATR for stops produced highest Sharpe in their crypto dataset — that is likely too tight for equities. Equities typically require 2–3x ATR. Start at 2.5x.
- Stale close: 48 bars (= 24 hours of 30-min bars) if no trigger fires. Li et al. 2026 found 48h stale close dominated 24h; do not close profitable positions too early.
tpsl.greeks_based:
OPTIONS GREEKS-BASED EXIT RULES (short-premium structures: short straddle, short strangle, iron condor, credit spread, short put/call):

RULE 1 — 50% Max Profit (tastylive heuristic, practitioner evidence):
- Close the entire structure when mark-to-market P&L >= 50% of the initial credit received (max profit for defined-risk structures is the full credit).
- Rationale: after 50% of premium is captured, the remaining expected P&L from holding to expiry is roughly balanced against the path risk of a spike reversing the position. Tastylive's internal research (segment: 'Managing Winners') found closing at 50% profit improved win rate and reduced variance vs. holding to expiry, at the cost of some average per-trade credit. This is practitioner-lore from a proprietary study with no peer-reviewed methodology disclosure. It is the most widely used heuristic in retail short-premium trading.
- STATUS: EVAL-GATE-PENDING on AEGIS data. Apply only after the 60-day / N>=100 options evidence window.

RULE 2 — 21 DTE (tastylive heuristic):
- For options opened at 45 DTE (the standard tastylive entry), close at 21 DTE regardless of P&L. Rationale: gamma accelerates relative to theta inside 21 DTE; the risk/reward for short-premium deteriorates. This is particularly important for structures near the short strikes.
- Academic support (partial): Huang et al. 2025 (arXiv:2501.12397) found that for Iron Condors, the optimal stopping time tau generally falls in the range [50%–75%] of total duration (i.e., for a 45-DTE trade, exit between DTE 11–22). This is consistent with the 21 DTE heuristic on a mathematical basis. Their result holds for the 'not-left-biased' SPX Iron Condor variant.
- STATUS: EVAL-GATE-PENDING; the Huang et al. result is for symmetric structures and does not directly transfer to directional or asymmetric structures.

RULE 3 — Delta Breach (real-time greeks monitoring):
- For a short put (delta target: -0.15 to -0.20 at entry): close if delta magnitude exceeds 0.40 (i.e., the short put is now nearly at-the-money). Rationale: a delta breach from 0.15 to 0.40 means the position has moved ~1.5 standard deviations against you; remaining theta is insufficient to offset the delta-driven mark-to-market loss.
- For a short strangle opened at 0.15 delta each side: close the tested side (or full structure) when either short strikes crosses 0.30 delta.
- The delta-breach rule ACTS EARLIER than a fixed-$ stop on a short-premium structure because options P&L is nonlinear — a delta breach at 0.40 typically corresponds to a loss of 1–2x the initial credit (i.e., a 100–200% max-loss blowout is approaching but has not yet occurred).
- STATUS: EVAL-GATE-PENDING. The specific delta thresholds (0.40 for individual short options, 0.30 for strangle) are practitioner-norm, not studied thresholds.

RULE 4 — Loss Cap (2x credit received = max stop for defined-risk):
- For a credit spread or iron condor: NEVER let the loss exceed 2x the initial credit received. At a loss of 2x credit, close regardless of DTE or delta. Rationale: max theoretical loss for a credit spread = (spread width - credit), but in practice a 2x credit stop limits realized loss to a defined multiple without requiring real-time monitoring of the spread's full mark-to-market path.
- For AEGIS this should be wired as a hard rule (not a soft preference), consistent with the fail-CLOSED posture. The defined-risk structure IS the structural stop, but 2x-credit provides a tighter functional stop that acts before the wings.

RULE 5 — DTE-Correlated Tightening:
- Inside 21 DTE, tighten all delta-breach thresholds by one step (e.g., close at 0.30 instead of 0.40) because gamma risk accelerates. This is the academically supported finding from Huang et al. 2025 that near-expiry monitoring must intensify.
tpsl.options_specific:
HOW OPTIONS TP/SL DIFFERS STRUCTURALLY FROM EQUITY:

1. DEFINED-RISK = THE STRUCTURE IS THE HARD STOP (for debit spreads / long options / iron condors):
- For a long debit spread: the premium paid IS the maximum loss. There is no additional stop-loss to wire — you cannot lose more than you paid. The 'stop' is enforced by the structure at expiry.
- For a credit spread (short-premium, defined-risk): max loss = spread width - credit received. You are short premium up to that cap. A 2x-credit stop (Rule 4 above) is a tighter functional stop that fires before the structure's maximum loss is reached.
- For undefined-risk structures (short straddle, short strangle, naked put/call): there IS no structural stop; a hard-dollar or delta-breach stop MUST be wired. AEGIS posture requires that these structures not be permitted without a greeks-based close rule. Per the 60-day / N>=100 gate, naked shorts are default-OFF.

2. THETA DECAY IS THE P&L DRIVER (not directional price move):
- Unlike equity where P&L is proportional to price move, short-premium options P&L accrues via time decay. The 'take-profit' is earned continuously (theta per day), not at a single price target.
- Implication: a take-profit at 50% of credit CAN be reached with the underlying going nowhere (pure theta harvest). This means the TP trigger can fire much earlier than an equity R-multiple TP on an equivalent capital-at-risk basis.

3. GAMMA RISK REPLACES DELTA RISK NEAR EXPIRY:
- Inside 21 DTE, gamma (rate of change of delta per $1 move) overtakes theta. A previously profitable position can blow out rapidly on a sharp move. This is the quantitative basis for the 21 DTE rule.
- The DTE-based exit is effectively a TIME-TRIGGERED TRAILING STOP: it forces exit when remaining theta is insufficient to compensate for gamma exposure.

4. ASSIGNMENT RISK (American-style options / dividend dates):
- Short calls / puts can be exercised early, especially: (a) deep ITM options where time value < dividend about to be paid (for short calls), or (b) short puts when the cost of carrying the stock exceeds remaining extrinsic value.
- AEGIS mitigations: (i) do not hold short calls through ex-dividend dates on dividend-paying stocks; (ii) close any short that goes deep ITM (delta > 0.80) before the option loses all extrinsic value; (iii) wire an automated early-assignment detector that flags when extrinsic value < transaction cost threshold and fires a close.
- Practical rule: close any short option where extrinsic value <= $0.10 (or 5% of the original credit, whichever is larger). This effectively prevents assignment scenarios.

5. SLIPPAGE AND BID-ASK ON OPTIONS IS QUALITATIVELY DIFFERENT:
- Options bid-ask spreads are typically 5–15% of option value for liquid equities and index options (vs. 0.01–0.05% for equities). This means the effective stop-loss for options has a structurally wider threshold than the paper-computed level.
- The AEGIS slippage haircut (ADR-0097 / aegis-sl01) must be applied to options exits, and the haircut will be LARGER than for equity exits. Do not copy equity-calibrated stop widths to options.

6. THE 50% PROFIT RULE PRODUCES MORE OCCURRENCES (the tastylive argument):
- By closing at 50% max profit instead of holding to expiry, the position turn-around time is halved on average, meaning more positions can be placed per year from the same capital, increasing the number of realized events and improving the statistical quality of the evidence window faster. This is the meta-rationale for using 50% rather than 100%: it is a capital-velocity optimization, not just a risk-reduction rule.
tpsl.defaults:
CONCRETE STARTING NUMBERS (all flagged by evidence level):

--- EQUITY (NAV-fraction ladder) ---

Hard Stop:
- 8% below entry (or 8% of entry price; maps to ~0.4R on a 0.10 NAV position with 20% expected move)
- EVAL-GATE-PENDING: this matches AEGIS current 8% stop parameter. Li et al. 2026 found 10% superior to 25% in crypto; for equities a tighter range of 6–12% is reasonable. Eval-gate on own data.

Hard Take-Profit (all-at-once default):
- +1R = entry + (stop distance) x 1.0 (i.e., symmetric risk/reward)
- If position = 0.10 NAV and stop is 8%, TP is 8% above entry.
- EVAL-GATE-PENDING: the R-multiple must be calibrated per strategy. The symmetric 1R TP is a conservative starting point.

Trailing Activation:
- Activate trailing stop only after position is up >= 3% from entry.
- EVIDENCED (Li et al. 2026, top-5 configurations all used 3% activation): this is the most consistent finding across all five top configurations.

Trailing Distance (hard-stop trailing, not ATR):
- 5–7% for full position; 3–5% for residual tranche.
- EVAL-GATE-PENDING: Li et al. found 2–3% trailing distance optimal in crypto (high-volatility) — likely too tight for equities. 5–7% is a conservative upward adjustment.

ATR Multiplier for Chandelier:
- N = 2.5 x ATR(14 bars, 30-min) — EVAL-GATE-PENDING.
- Li et al. 2026 found N=1.0x optimal in crypto (highest Sharpe); for equities 2–3x is the practitioner standard. Start at 2.5x, eval-gate.

Tranche 1 TP (scale-out):
- Exit first ladder step (0.05 NAV) at +1R unrealized.
- EVAL-GATE-PENDING.

Tranche 2 TP or trail:
- Exit residual at +2R OR trailing stop, whichever fires first.
- EVAL-GATE-PENDING.

Stale Close:
- 48 bars (24 hours at 30-min cadence) if no other trigger fires.
- EVIDENCED direction (Li et al. 2026: 48h dominated 24h across all top-5 configs), though the specific 48h number is calibrated to a different asset class and regime — treat as directional evidence, not a point estimate.

--- OPTIONS (short premium, defined-risk) ---

Profit Target:
- 50% of initial credit received.
- EVIDENCED (tastylive practitioner research, Huang et al. 2025 mathematical support for 50–75% of duration window). Flag: tastylive study is proprietary with no disclosed methodology; use 50% as a starting default and eval-gate on our own data.

DTE-based close:
- 21 DTE for options entered at 40–45 DTE.
- EVIDENCED (Huang et al. 2025: optimal tau in [50–75%] of total duration for symmetric Iron Condors in SPX; 21/45 = 47%, just below their 50% lower bound — treat as broadly consistent).

Loss cap:
- 2x initial credit received (hard stop).
- EVIDENCED in mechanism (defined-risk structural cap), but 2x multiplier is practitioner-norm with no specific academic study.

Delta breach threshold:
- Close if short delta magnitude exceeds 0.40 (pre-21 DTE) or 0.30 (inside 21 DTE).
- EVAL-GATE-PENDING (practitioner-norm, no peer-reviewed threshold study).

Extrinsic value floor (assignment prevention):
- Close any short option where extrinsic value <= $0.10 or 5% of original credit.
- EVAL-GATE-PENDING (practitioner standard, conservative).

60-day / N>=100 evidence window for live options:
- STANDING GATE from AEGIS posture: no options strategy goes live without this evidence window. All options-specific numbers above are DEFAULT-OFF until that gate is met.
tpsl.adversarial:
ADVERSARIAL CASE AGAINST EACH METHOD:

AGAINST TRAILING STOPS (whipsaw / premature liquidation):
- The core problem is that a trailing stop optimized on historical data is essentially fitting to the noise signature of that specific regime. Kaminski & Lo (2014, Journal of Financial Markets) demonstrate that stop-loss rules based on trailing drawdowns provide negative alpha in trending regimes that recover (they exit the position right before recovery). Their key finding: stop-loss rules reduce variance but ALSO reduce mean return, and the Sharpe improvement is inconsistent across market regimes. A stop-loss that works in a trending market will whipsaw repeatedly in a sideways-volatile market.
- Glynn & Iglehart (1995, Management Science) show analytically that a trailing stop at percentage p loses value relative to a simple buy-and-hold position in a pure GBM world when the drift is positive and p is set tightly — the only regimes where trailing stops clearly win are those with fat-tailed reversals, not the GBM baseline.
- Dai et al. (2021, International Review of Finance) — cited in Li et al. 2026 — found trailing stops reduce RISK but do not consistently improve RISK-ADJUSTED returns. Their title ('Risk reduction using trailing stop-loss rules') is self-descriptive: they reduce drawdown, not Sharpe.
- THRESHOLD TO AVOID: Trailing distance < 5% on a 30-min equity signal. At that width, the stop is inside the bid-ask noise plus intra-bar volatility, and it will fire randomly.

AGAINST SCALE-OUT TRANCHES (tranching reduces winners):
- A mathematical identity: if your trade is a winner at +2R and you have already exited half at +1R, your realized average exit is 1.5R. If you had held all and exited at +2R, you would have collected 2R. Tranching always reduces the realized return on full winners.
- The only scenario where tranching outperforms all-at-once is when the distribution of winners has a mass that peaks at +1R and then reverses — i.e., +1R is the mode of the winner distribution. If the winner distribution is fat-tailed (momentum), holding to +2R and beyond is better.
- The Li et al. 2026 finding that 75% partial take-profit fraction (exit 75% at the first threshold) outperforms 25% / 50% is consistent with this: on their crypto dataset, prices rarely ran beyond the first TP, so banking 75% early was better than keeping 75% for a larger target that rarely came. This is regime-specific and may not apply to AEGIS equity positions.
- The incremental complexity of tracking multiple tranche levels, tranche sizes, and per-tranche trailing logic creates material implementation risk in a money-software system. Each added state variable is a new class of bugs (e.g., ar13/ar14 style unit-vs-NAV-fraction errors, cs14 stale-schema reads).

AGAINST ALL-AT-ONCE (leaves residual profit on the table):
- The pure binary stop/TP design does not differentiate between a position that barely crossed the hard stop (noisy reversal) and one that crossed it on true adverse momentum. Both are closed at the same level. This is a coarse response to a continuous signal.
- With a thin history (< 60 sessions), the R-multiple TP target has no statistical backing — it is a free parameter, not a calibrated number. An incorrectly set TP at +0.5R on a momentum strategy means you are systematically undershooting winners.

AGAINST GREEKS-BASED EXITS (thin data / model risk):
- Delta and gamma values depend on the IV used in the pricing model. If the IV surface is mis-estimated (common for low-liquidity strikes), delta-breach rules can fire on model artifacts rather than real risk.
- The 50% profit and 21 DTE rules emerged from tastylive's in-house research on SPX options in a post-2010 low-volatility regime. Their applicability to (a) individual equities rather than SPX, (b) higher-volatility regimes like 2022 or 2025, and (c) smaller notional sizes where bid-ask spreads eat more of the collected premium, is not established.
- The Huang et al. 2025 optimal-stopping result for Iron Condors assumes a Rough Heston model and a bounded martingale. Neither assumption is guaranteed to hold in real markets during tail events. Their 50–75% of duration window is a central-case result, not a tail-event result.

AGAINST TIME-BASED EXITS (arbitrary regime ignoring):
- DTE-based exits close positions based on a calendar rule that is completely independent of market state. In a trend period, closing a profitable strangle at 21 DTE sacrifices theta that would have been collected pain-free. In a crisis, 21 DTE may still be inside a sharp move with a live delta exposure that should have been closed earlier.
sources: Li, N., Laryea, A., Ihlamur, Y. (2026). 'Optimal Stop-Loss and Take-Profit Parameterization for Autonomous Trading Agent Swarm.' arXiv:2604.27150. — 8,960-configuration grid search on 900+ crypto trades; found SL=10%, trailing activation=3%, trailing distance=3–5%, partial TP fraction=75%, 48h stale close, ATR multiplier 1.0x stop / 2.0x TP as strongest first-pass + second-pass configurations. Key: 56% Sharpe improvement over 25% baseline SL. NOTE: crypto, randomized (not chronological) evaluation protocol; results are directional, not numerically portable to equities.

Kaminski, K.M. and Lo, A.W. (2014). 'When do stop-loss rules stop losses?' Journal of Financial Markets, 18, 234–254. — Systematic study of when stop-loss rules help vs. hurt across regimes. Finding: stop-loss rules reduce variance and max drawdown but reduce mean return; Sharpe improvement is regime-dependent and not robust across asset classes. Adversarial finding directly relevant to AEGIS. Full text paywalled; cited via arXiv:2604.27150 and multiple secondary sources.

Glynn, P.W. and Iglehart, D.L. (1995). 'Trading Securities Using Trailing Stops.' Management Science, 41(6), 1096–1106. — Analytical result: trailing stops cost value vs. buy-and-hold in a GBM world with positive drift. The benefit only materializes with fat-tailed adverse scenarios.

Dai, B., Marshall, B.R., Nguyen, N.H., Visaltanachoti, N. (2021). 'Risk reduction using trailing stop-loss rules.' International Review of Finance, 21(4), 1334–1352. — Empirical finding: trailing stops reduce risk (drawdown) but do not consistently improve risk-adjusted returns. Cited in arXiv:2604.27150.

Huang, H., Sun, Q., Yang, X. (2025). 'Stochastic Optimal Control of Iron Condor Portfolios for Profitability and Risk Management.' arXiv:2501.12397. — Mathematical proof that for symmetric Iron Condors with a bounded martingale underlying, optimal exit tau = T (hold to expiry). For general (asymmetric, DOTM) scenarios via Rough Heston simulation, optimal tau falls in [50%–75%] of total duration. Case-validated on SPX data across bull/sideways/bear.

Leung, T. and Li, X. (2015). 'Optimal Mean Reversion Trading with Transaction Costs and Stop-Loss Exit.' International Journal of Theoretical and Applied Finance, 18(3). arXiv:1411.5062. — Analytical framework: for mean-reverting spread trading, higher stop-loss level forces lower optimal take-profit level; entry region is bounded above the stop-loss level.

Journal of Portfolio Management, 40(5), 94–107. — Directly applicable caution: large parameter searches on finite historical samples (like exit parameter grids) are subject to multiple-testing bias. The Li et al. 2026 paper explicitly cites this as a limitation.

Core claims: closing short-premium positions at 50% of max profit improves win rate and capital velocity; 21 DTE is the gamma/theta crossover for 45-DTE entries on SPX. NOTE: these studies are proprietary with no disclosed methodology and should be treated as practitioner-lore, not academic evidence.

'Follow the Leader: Enhancing Systematic Trend-Following Using Network Momentum.' arXiv:2501.07135. — Evidence that trend-following strategies exhibit positive-skew return distributions (regular small losses compensated by fewer large gains); consistent with trailing-stop design rationale where letting winners run is the key alpha source.

multileg.model:
RECOMMENDED 2-LEVEL MULTI-LEG MODEL

The composite multi-leg play AND its individual legs coexist in the bus, ledger, and monitor:

LEVEL-1 (COMPOSITE): One ExecutionRecord per family, asset_class="multi_leg", asset=underlying. Carries: multi_leg_id (= proposal_id), strategy_kind, outer_qty, net_greeks, net_fill (signed net_debit/credit), fill_size_pct (NAV-fraction sized against the whole structure), role="parent". Contains no position-moving quantity. It is an AUDIT ROLLUP only — the PortfolioState fold SKIPS it (_is_multileg_family_parent).

LEVEL-2 (LEGS): N child ExecutionRecords per family, one per leg. Each child carries: its own asset (OCC-21 symbol), its own asset_class ("us_option" or "equity"), the same multi_leg_id (back-link to the composite), leg_index, role ("leg"/"equity_leg"), signed true-unit quantity (contracts/shares), fill_price (per-share/per-contract premium), position_intent (buy_to_open / sell_to_open / ...), ratio_qty. These ARE position-moving. The fold reads ONLY children.

RISK MONITOR watches BOTH levels simultaneously:
  - Composite-level: net_greeks (delta/gamma/theta/vega), net BPR, max_loss on the STRUCTURE. Gate-sized at composite level (OptionsGateResult.contracts is the outer_qty; BPR is the structure's collective margin requirement). This is the FIRST gate — structure-level greek caps (ADR-0027 D6).
  - Leg-level: each child contributes to the equity_total fold (PortfolioState) independently via its FIFO position tracking. The monitor watches each leg's unrealized P&L and breach thresholds independently for DECOMPOSE trigger detection.
multileg.composite_vs_legs:
COMPOSITE is parent_id authority. All leg records carry reactor_metadata.multi_leg_id = proposal_id as the tie (a string foreign key on the append-only bus). Leg roles are discriminated by reactor_metadata.role:
  "parent"      — composite audit rollup (SKIP in fold)
  "leg"         — option leg child (us_option; position-moving)
  "equity_leg"  — stock leg child of a covered call (equity; position-moving)

GATE SIZES at composite level: OptionsGateResult.contracts = outer_qty. BPR and max_loss are structure-level (sum of margin requirements across legs, not per-leg). The gate accepts or rejects the WHOLE structure atomically — a partial-leg pass is not defined.

MONITOR WATCHES at BOTH levels:
  - Composite-level monitor: net_greeks snap from the parent record's reactor_metadata.net_greeks. Refresh on each tick by re-evaluating via aggregate_net_greeks(live_leg_prices) — not from the stale parent snapshot. Composite-level P&L = Σ leg P&Ls.
  - Leg-level monitor: PortfolioState.get_positions() returns each leg under its own (asset_class, symbol) key. The per-leg unrealized P&L is (current_price - avg_entry_price) * quantity * multiplier. The leg-level monitor detects individual leg breaches that trigger DECOMPOSE rules.

KEY INVARIANT: a position exists in the ledger ONLY at leg level. The composite exists ONLY in the bus (executions.jsonl) and in a separate composite_plays table (see data model). There is NO duplicate position entry for the composite in the positions table — violating this is the double-count hazard (cs44).
multileg.decompose_rules:
Deterministic. Decompose (break the composite into independently-managed legs) when ANY of:

RULE D1 — SHORT LEG ASSIGNMENT: The broker notifies that a short leg (sell_to_open position) has been assigned (exercised against). This transforms that leg from an option position to a stock obligation OUTSIDE the original structure. Trigger: assignment event from broker (Alpaca order status = "assigned" or broker fill with trigger="assignment"). Action: mark composite as decomposed (composite_plays.state = "decomposed"); the assigned leg's obligation is now a standalone equity/short position; the remaining legs become orphan-tracked standalone positions. NO new mleg order is permitted on a decomposed composite — any adjustment must go through individual leg orders.

RULE D2 — THESIS INVALIDATION ON ONE LEG: The risk committee (LLM evidence-only, never amplifies) produces a silence signal for one leg's underlying while other legs remain actionable. The operator receives a DECOMPOSE recommendation. This is operator-gated: NEVER autonomous. The agent may RECOMMEND decompose; the operator APPROVES via HITL (quant_approve).

RULE D3 — LEG BREACHES OWN STOP-LOSS THRESHOLD: A child leg's unrealized P&L as a NAV-fraction breaches its own stop-loss threshold (e.g. the short put in a vertical spread reaches max-loss 90% territory) AND the net composite P&L has not yet triggered the composite stop. Because the risk-limiting leg (the long put) should theoretically limit the loss, a per-leg stop-loss breach on a DEFINED-RISK structure is only operator-gated (see CONVERT rule C2 for rolling the losing leg instead). On an UNDEFINED-RISK leg (naked leg that slipped past gate — should never happen with gate-is-final-authority but defence-in-depth applies), decompose is IMMEDIATE and autonomous.

RULE D4 — PARTIAL FILL ON OPEN: If the broker fills only some legs of a submitted mleg order (partial legs filled, some legs rejected), the successfully-filled legs become standalone positions and the composite is never formed. The parent record is written as no-fill; filled leg children are written as standalone fills with no multi_leg_id (or a decomposed-at-birth flag).

RULE D5 — EXPIRATION MISMATCH EVENT: On calendar spreads, if one leg expires and the other has not, the composite is automatically decomposed at leg expiry. The remaining leg becomes a standalone position.

NOTE: DECOMPOSE never happens partially without operator approval on defined-risk structures. D1 (assignment) is the only autonomous trigger on a defined-risk structure; D4 (partial fill) is structural, not a decision.
multileg.convert_rules:
A CONVERT is an in-place restructuring: close one or more legs and open new ones, replacing the composite with a new composite. All conversions are subject to: (a) atomicity constraint — the close and open must be submitted as a single HITL-approved mleg or sequential leg orders with a new proposal_id; (b) cost constraint — the net debit/credit of the convert must stay within the gate-approved BPR of the new structure; (c) the OLD composite must be fully closed before the NEW composite is opened (no overlapping legs on the same OCC symbol with conflicting position_intent).

CONVERT RULE C1 — ROLL A VERTICAL (same-width, different strike/expiry):
WHEN: the short leg of a vertical spread approaches expiry (DTE <= N, typically 21 DTE) AND the structure is profitable (net credit received > 50% of max credit). HOW: submit a 4-leg mleg: close old short (buy_to_close), close old long (sell_to_close), open new short (sell_to_open, further expiry), open new long (buy_to_open, same width). ATOMICITY: single Alpaca mleg order with order_class="mleg", 4 legs. The old composite is NOT decomposed until the new mleg fills. On fill, the old composite is closed (reactor writes 4 child records with the old multi_leg_id as "close" children) and a NEW proposal_id anchors the new composite + its children. COST CONSTRAINT: the net cost of the roll (net debit of the 4-leg order) must be <= 0 (ideally a credit roll) for it to pass the gate.

CONVERT RULE C2 — LEG INTO DIFFERENT STRUCTURE (e.g. tested short put -> spread):
WHEN: a short put (CSP) is tested (underlying moves against the position, short put approaches the money) and the operator wants to add a long put below it to cap risk. HOW: submit a 2-leg mleg: buy_to_open the protective put + optionally sell_to_close the original short put and sell_to_open a higher-strike short put (re-center). ATOMICITY: single Alpaca mleg order; if the original CSP was a single-leg order, the CONVERT converts it to a spread by adding a leg without closing the old. The old CSP's ExecutionRecord is NOT closed — a new multi_leg_id is minted that references the original leg via a "converted_from" field in the new composite's reactor_metadata. COST CONSTRAINT: the long put premium paid reduces the credit collected by the original CSP; gate must re-admit the combined structure.

CONVERT RULE C3 — CLOSE-AND-REPLACE (same structure, new expiry cycle):
WHEN: the composite is approaching max profit (e.g. net_debit_credit has decayed to < 20% of original) and the operator wants to re-establish. HOW: submit a close of the existing composite (2-leg mleg buy_to_close + sell_to_close), then a separate NEW proposal for the replacement. These are TWO sequential proposals, not one atomic convert. The old composite closes completely before the new one opens.

ATOMICITY INVARIANT: on any convert, if the close legs fill but the open legs reject, the system is in a DECOMPOSED state (the old composite is closed, no new composite). The monitor must detect this leg-orphan state (no parent composite, some legs have open positions) and alert the operator. The gate must NOT automatically open the new composite if the old composite is only partially closed.
multileg.risk_adjust_rules:
RISK-ADJUST is a single-leg operation on a LIVE composite without decomposing or closing the structure. All risk-adjustments are operator-gated (never autonomous).

RAR-1 — CLOSE ONE LEG (take profit or stop-loss on one leg):
The operator approves a single-leg close order (buy_to_close or sell_to_close on one leg). A new single-leg proposal is created with the SAME multi_leg_id as the existing composite (so the settlement loop attributes the realized P&L to the family). The proposal kind = "equity" (single-leg) but reactor_metadata carries: {"multi_leg_id": "<parent_id>", "role": "leg_close", "closes_leg_index": N}. The child ExecutionRecord is written to the bus with the same multi_leg_id, linking it to the family. The composite is NOT decomposed — it continues to exist with one fewer active leg. The MONITOR updates: composite.net_greeks is recomputed from remaining open legs only.

RAR-2 — ROLL ONE LEG (close + reopen same leg at different strike/expiry):
Two sequential atomic steps:
  Step A: single buy_to_close or sell_to_close (position_intent = "*_to_close") — same as RAR-1 but position is fully closed first.
  Step B: single new sell_to_open or buy_to_open at the new strike/expiry — a new child ExecutionRecord with the SAME multi_leg_id, role="leg_roll", replaces_leg_index=N, new_leg_index=N.
The composite remains live throughout. The NET effect is: the old leg exits, the new leg enters, the composite's net_greeks and BPR are updated. Gate re-evaluation is required for step B (the new leg's greeks at decision must pass the structure's greek caps and BPR with the remaining existing legs).

RAR-3 — ADD A HEDGE LEG:
Buy a protective option on an existing open leg (e.g. buy a put to hedge a short call leg in a deteriorating CC). New single-leg proposal, role="hedge_leg", multi_leg_id=parent. Net greek recalculation after addition. COST: the hedge premium reduces net credit/increases net debit — the composite's max_loss may change from None (undefined for CC/CSP) to a defined value after adding the hedge.

ORPHAN PREVENTION: In all three cases, the parent composite record in composite_plays must be updated atomically with the leg modification. The update pattern:
  1. Claim the HITL approval (claim_for_approval CAS on the single-leg close proposal).
  2. Write the child ExecutionRecord to the bus.
  3. Update composite_plays: add the leg record to composite_plays.closed_leg_ids or .adjusted_leg_ids.
  4. Recompute and persist composite_plays.current_net_greeks.
Steps 2-4 must happen inside a single append_locked call (atomic family write) so a crash never leaves the composite in an unknown state. If step 3 fails, the composite shows a stale but safe greek snapshot — the monitor will recompute on the next tick.
multileg.data_model_sketch:
EXISTING LEDGER (unchanged):
  executions.jsonl: append-only JSONL; each line is an ExecutionRecord dict.
  state.db: positions table keyed on (account_id, asset_class, symbol); cash table; processed_fills dedup table.
  PortfolioState fold: reads ONLY leg children (skips asset_class=="multi_leg" parent).

NEW TABLE: composite_plays (in state.db, or a separate composite_plays.db)

CREATE TABLE composite_plays (
    multi_leg_id     TEXT    NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,  -- = proposal_id
    account_id       TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT 'paper-default',
    underlying       TEXT    NOT NULL,
    strategy_kind    TEXT    NOT NULL,
    state            TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT 'open',  -- open|decomposed|closed|partial
    opened_at        TEXT    NOT NULL,  -- ISO UTC
    closed_at        TEXT,              -- ISO UTC, NULL while open
    outer_qty        INTEGER NOT NULL,
    net_entry_price  REAL    NOT NULL,  -- net debit/credit at fill (signed)
    net_fill_price   REAL,              -- filled net (may differ from entry after roll)
    fill_size_pct    REAL    NOT NULL,  -- NAV fraction
    max_loss_usd     REAL,              -- NULL for undefined-risk structures
    bpr_usd          REAL    NOT NULL,
    risk_gate_bucket TEXT    NOT NULL,
    delta_at_open    REAL    NOT NULL,
    gamma_at_open    REAL    NOT NULL,
    theta_at_open    REAL    NOT NULL,
    vega_at_open     REAL    NOT NULL,
    current_delta    REAL,   -- refreshed each monitor tick; NULL = not yet refreshed
    current_gamma    REAL,
    current_theta    REAL,
    current_vega     REAL,
    play_tag         TEXT,   -- advisor|playbook|autonomous
    converted_from   TEXT,   -- multi_leg_id of prior composite if this is a convert
    record_json      TEXT    NOT NULL   -- full serialized MultiLegProposal payload (canonical)
) WITHOUT ROWID;

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_cp_account ON composite_plays(account_id, state);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_cp_underlying ON composite_plays(underlying, state);

LINKING LEGS TO COMPOSITE:
No separate join table. The executions.jsonl bus records carry multi_leg_id in reactor_metadata. To enumerate all legs of a composite: scan executions.jsonl for records with reactor_metadata.multi_leg_id == target AND role IN ("leg", "equity_leg", "leg_close", "leg_roll", "hedge_leg"). This is an O(N) scan bounded by the bus size — acceptable for an operator-facing monitor (not a hot tick path). For a hot-path greek refresh, composite_plays.current_delta/gamma/theta/vega are the denormalized cache.

FIFO / MULTIPLIER HANDLING:
  - us_option child: quantity = signed_contracts (e.g. -1 for short 1 contract); multiplier = 100. PortfolioState fold: delta_cash = -signed_qty * fill_price * 100. Position.quantity = signed_contracts.
  - equity child: quantity = signed_shares; multiplier = 1. PortfolioState fold: delta_cash = -signed_qty * fill_price * 1.
  - FIFO applies within EACH leg's (asset_class, symbol) position independently. A leg close record hits the SAME (asset_class, symbol) FIFO queue as the original leg open — the FIFO fold does NOT need to know about the multi_leg_id for realized P&L accounting. realized_return for the settlement loop = FIFO lot match per (asset_class, symbol).
  - The composite (asset_class="multi_leg") NEVER enters the positions table. composite_plays.net_fill_price - initial net_entry_price tracks composite-level P&L for monitoring/reflection, not for the FIFO ledger.

COMPOSITE KEY CONVENTION:
  executions.jsonl parent record: asset_class="multi_leg", asset=underlying (e.g. "AAPL").
  composite_plays PK: multi_leg_id (= proposal_id = "prop_<ISO>_<underlying>_<rand6>").
  No (asset_class, symbol) composite key is written to the positions table.
multileg.hazards:
H1 — LEG ORPHAN ON PARTIAL DECOMPOSE:
When a DECOMPOSE or CONVERT attempt closes some legs but the broker rejects the remaining leg orders, the bus contains close records for some legs but the composite is still "open" in composite_plays. The MONITOR detects orphan state: composite_plays.state == "open" BUT active_leg_count < expected_leg_count (computed by scanning the bus for open vs close records per multi_leg_id). MITIGATION: write the composite state as "partial" (not "open" or "closed") on the first leg close within a decompose sequence. A "partial" composite triggers mandatory operator attention. Never auto-close a composite that is in "partial" state.

H2 — DOUBLE-COUNTING A LEG AT BOTH LEVELS:
If the composite (multi_leg, underlying) record were ever folded into the positions table, it would create a phantom "multi_leg" position AND double-count cash (the parent's fill_price is the net credit/debit but has no multiplier anchor). This is the cs44 defect, fixed by _is_multileg_family_parent skip in BOTH folds (reconstruct_from and _apply_execution_unsafe). The discriminator is asset_class == "multi_leg" on the ExecutionRecord — this value MUST remain parent-ONLY; no child may use it. MITIGATION: the _MULTILEG_PARENT_ASSET_CLASS constant is the single source of truth; any new producer path must use "us_option"/"equity" for children, never "multi_leg".

H3 — LEDGER FOLD SEEING LEG VS COMPOSITE:
The settlement_loop computes realized P&L per SettledRoundTrip. If a settlement-loop consumer reads the bus naively and includes the parent record in the kill-switch basis, the net_fill on the parent (the net credit/debit of the structure) is in DIFFERENT UNITS than the child records (child: per-share/per-contract; parent: net_fill is the total net debit/credit of the structure). The ar34 family (cross-account filtering) and the ar25 kill-switch basis bug (parent qty already NAV-fraction vs child qty in true-units) both trace here. MITIGATION: the settlement_loop must filter parent records by the same _is_multileg_family_parent skip, OR by requiring multi_leg_id != None AND role == "parent" → skip. The settlement loop's SettledRoundTrip must be computed on LEGS ONLY, matched by (asset_class, symbol) FIFO.

H4 — FOLD ATOMICITY ON CONVERT:
A CONVERT requires closing old legs AND opening new legs. If the bus write is interrupted between the close records and the open records (e.g. process crash after writing leg-close ExecutionRecords but before the new composite's ExecutionRecords), the reconstruct_from rebuild will see: old composite "open" in composite_plays, some close records present. MITIGATION: composite_plays.state is set to "converting" (an intermediate state) before the close leg writes begin. On startup, any "converting" composite gets operator review. The new multi_leg_id is only written to composite_plays AFTER all new leg opens are written to the bus. The bus write uses a single append_locked call for the full set (close records + new parent + new children) — atomic at the flock level.

H5 — MONITOR DOUBLE-NETTING GREEKS:
If the monitor naively sums composite.current_delta across all open composites AND also sums each leg's standalone delta from PortfolioState (for non-composite equity positions), it may double-count the delta of composite legs (the composite delta is already the sum of leg deltas). MITIGATION: the portfolio-level greek aggregation must choose ONE level: either enumerate composites from composite_plays (and use composite.current_delta/gamma/theta/vega summed with standalone non-composite positions) OR enumerate PortfolioState positions individually AND skip the composite_plays table entirely. The two levels must never be summed together. AEGIS should use: composite_plays for composite-level Greek monitoring; PortfolioState for position counting (cash, NAV, kill-switch P&L basis). These two are complementary, not additive.

H6 — ROLL ATOMICITY (OLD COMPOSITE NOT CLOSED BEFORE NEW OPENS):
During a C2 convert (add-leg to CSP to make a spread), if the new long put is bought before the original short put is repriced/repositioned, there is a window where the book shows TWO positions on the same underlying's option chain but only ONE composite_plays row. MITIGATION: require that the operator explicitly closes the old composite (as a "converting" state) before any new composite on the same underlying + strategy_kind opens.
