heuristic.recommendation:
A three-gate hierarchy governs the clean-window record before any unlock:

GATE-0 (reset prerequisite, operator-executed before clock starts): Run quant-reset-paper-book --apply to flatten the book to $100k. Arm all four protective flags in the cron wrapper (HERMES_QUANT_DURABLE_DRAWDOWN_BASELINE=1, PER_POSITION_STOP=1, DELTA_NORMALIZER=1, ACCOUNT_LOCK=1). Enable the slippage haircut (HERMES_QUANT_PAPER_SLIPPAGE_MODEL=v0.2 is already on; verify). The clean window clock starts ONLY after this gate executes. Any metric computed before GATE-0 is poisoned data and must be discarded. The prior 0/11 (-4.64%) record is pre-GATE-0 and carries zero statistical weight.

GATE-1 (not-obviously-broken / keep-running signal, N>=20 round trips): win_rate >= 0.40 (Wilson CI lower bound clears 0), no kill-switch fires, rolling_30d_max_drawdown <= 8% NAV. This is a SURVIVAL gate. Failure here triggers a strategy review or parameter change, NOT a live consideration unlock. Passing is necessary but not sufficient for anything further. Estimated calendar time: 2-4 weeks depending on trade frequency.

GATE-2 (preliminary edge / options-HITL-paper unlock, N>=50 round trips AND >= 60 calendar days since GATE-0): profit_factor_point_estimate >= 1.3 (point only; CI is too wide at N=50 to require), win_rate >= 0.50, rolling_90d_sharpe_point_estimate >= 0.8 (annualized, daily returns basis), max_consecutive_losses <= 8, zero immutable-rule breaches. This unlocks HITL-paper options (proposal + human approval loop only, per ADR-0029 D6). It does NOT unlock autonomous options or live. Estimated calendar time: 4-10 weeks post-GATE-0.

GATE-3 (full live promotion, the existing ADR-0029/live.py gate): N>=100 settled round trips, sharpe_95ci_lower >= 1.0 (stationary block bootstrap on all daily returns since GATE-0, per evaluation/validation.py), rolling_30d_max_drawdown <= 1% NAV, no kill-switch in trailing 14d, zero immutable-rule breaches in 30d, calibrator drift <= 5%. The LiveTradingApproval Pydantic model (hermes_quant/react/live.py) already enforces this. GATE-3 passing implicitly satisfies the ADR-0029 D7 options live criteria IF N_options >= 100 (counted separately from equity round trips).

The CI implementation note: AEGIS uses stationary block bootstrap (Politis-Romano 1994, block-length auto-selected per Politis-White 2004 with Patton correction) as PRIMARY, plus BCa secondary. This is TIGHTER than the Lo 2002 iid formula (which gives CI width ~±1.1 at N=100 daily observations). The block bootstrap accounts for serial autocorrelation in returns, which the Lo formula cannot. A 30-day Sharpe CI_lower >= 1.0 from the block bootstrap requires highly consistent daily returns with low variance -- achievable in paper with no market impact, which is intentional: the gate is calibrated for paper inflation.
metrics: win_rate (settled round trips): primary evidence metric. Directional: > 0.50 gate-2, > 0.55 preferred. Use Wilson score CI to verify the lower bound clears zero before counting N=20 sample as meaningful. Rationale: sign-correct at the individual-trade level regardless of P&L magnitude; works identically for stock and options trades when defined against the settled outcome.

realized_sharpe_annualized (daily returns basis, rolling window): computed as mean_daily_return / std_daily_return * sqrt(252), matching ADR-0029 implementation. Point estimate used for GATE-2 threshold (>= 0.8); bootstrap CI lower bound (>= 1.0) used for GATE-3. Rationale: single most-cited risk-adjusted performance metric; stationary block bootstrap correctly handles the serial correlation in daily returns that the iid Lo formula ignores.

sharpe_95ci_lower (stationary block bootstrap, BCa secondary): the ADR-0029 LIVE gate metric. Must be >= 1.0 on the full daily-return history since GATE-0. Key caveat: at T=30 daily returns the Lo approximation gives CI width ~±5.8 making this nearly impossible by formula alone; the block bootstrap achieves narrower CI for autocorrelated sequences. N_days >= 252 is needed for this to clear 1.0 at point Sharpe ~2.0 under Lo; the block bootstrap can clear it earlier for consistent return series.

profit_factor (gross_wins / gross_losses, per settled round trips): PF >= 1.3 point estimate at N=50 (GATE-2 unlock). PF CI is too wide at N=50 (95% CI lower ~0.67 at PF=1.5) to gate on the lower bound; use point estimate only at GATE-2. At N=100, PF >= 1.5 has CI_lower ~0.91 (approaching significance). Rationale: robust to heavy tails where Sharpe is distorted; directly interpretable as 'each dollar lost generates X dollars won'.

max_consecutive_losses (count): GATE-2 ceiling of 8. Rationale: long losing streaks signal regime mismatch or strategy failure independent of Sharpe; at N=50 trades, 8 consecutive losses = 1-in-(2^8)=0.4% probability under 50% win rate (significant signal). No formal academic citation; practitioner consensus (Bailey-LdP 2014 implicitly captures this via skewness/kurtosis adjustment).

rolling_30d_max_drawdown_pct (NAV fraction): 8% cap at GATE-1 (survival), 3% cap at GATE-2 (edge signal), 1% cap at GATE-3 (live gate, per live.py). Rationale: ADR-0016 kill-switch is realized-only; the drawdown metric catches open-position bleeding (the ASTS -20.9% failure mode) NOW that DURABLE_DRAWDOWN_BASELINE is armed.

DSR (Deflated Sharpe Ratio, n_trials=1): use the existing evaluation/dsr.py implementation as a SUPPLEMENTARY signal in the weekly retro. For a forward-only single-strategy window, n_trials=1 (no strategy search), so DSR reduces to PSR (Probabilistic Sharpe Ratio). At N=100 round trips, ann_SR=1.5: t-stat ~ 1.37, PSR ~ 0.915. Requires DSR >= 0.90 as a GATE-3 advisory (not a hard block, since the block-bootstrap CI is the primary). For multiple recipe variants tried: increment n_trials in dsr.deflated_sharpe call.

N_settled_round_trips (count): minimum count gate. N >= 20 (GATE-1), N >= 50 (GATE-2), N >= 100 (GATE-3). For options: N >= 100 multi-leg outcomes counted separately from equity (ADR-0029 D7). Rationale: Lo 2002 shows SR estimate standard error decreases as sqrt(N); the binomial CI on win_rate is similarly proportional to 1/sqrt(N). Below N=20 the CIs are so wide (win_rate CI width ~50%) that no metric is meaningful.
heuristic.thresholds:
GATE-1 thresholds (eval-gate-pending, N>=20 round trips from clean reset): win_rate >= 0.40, rolling_30d_max_drawdown_pct <= 0.08, kill_switch_fires == 0. These are below the ADR-0029 floors intentionally -- GATE-1 is a survive-or-reset signal, not an edge signal.

GATE-2 thresholds (eval-gate-pending, N>=50 round trips AND >= 60 calendar days): profit_factor_point >= 1.3, win_rate >= 0.50, rolling_90d_sharpe_point_estimate >= 0.8, max_consecutive_losses <= 8, rolling_30d_max_drawdown_pct <= 0.03, immutable_breaches_in_window == 0. Unlocks: options HITL-paper origination discussion (NOT autonomous, NOT live).

GATE-3 thresholds (live gate, existing ADR-0029/live.py enforcement): paper_outcomes_count >= 100, sharpe_95ci_lower >= 1.0 (bootstrap), rolling_30d_max_drawdown_pct <= 0.01, no_killswitch_in_trailing_14d == True, immutable_breaches_in_window == 0, calibrator_drift <= 0.05. These values are ALREADY HARDCODED in hermes_quant/react/live.py:LIVE_APPROVAL_THRESHOLDS and enforced by the LiveTradingApproval Pydantic model validator. Do NOT change them.

Relationship to ADR-0125 promotion floors: ADR-0125 does not yet exist as a file (the highest existing ADR is ADR-0097). The GATE-3 thresholds above ARE what ADR-0125 would formalize. They are already implemented in live.py. The reference in the operator packet to 'ar125' denotes the bug fix to the settlement-derived paper_outcomes_count computation, NOT a new ADR number.

Relationship to ADR-0029 D7 options window: ADR-0029 D7 requires 60+ trading days of multi-leg activity AND the live.py thresholds before live multi-leg. The GATE-2 unlock (options HITL-paper) is a NEW gate below ADR-0029 D7. This means the ordering is: GATE-0 -> GATE-1 (stocks only, no options) -> GATE-2 (options HITL-paper enabled) -> [60 trading days of options paper + N>=100 options outcomes] -> GATE-3 live promotion (requires LiveTradingApproval).

Statistical caution on all thresholds: All GATE-1 and GATE-2 thresholds are EVAL-GATE-PENDING. They represent starting points calibrated from Lo 2002 asymptotic theory and Bailey-LdP 2014 DSR analysis on a thin (N=50-100) forward-only sample with a single strategy and no multiple-comparison penalty. They must be validated against at least two full clean-window runs before being treated as fixed policy. Flag in ADR as provisional: threshold_status=eval-gate-pending-two-clean-windows.
heuristic.stock_vs_options_parity:
The operator ask is: stock AND options plays equally considered in the Decide phase, but properly differentiated downstream. The correct implementation:

DECIDE PHASE (equal treatment): The PDR deliberative committee (ADR-0023) receives both stock Proposals and MultiLegProposals on equal footing. Neither is privileged in the committee vote. The committee votes on EXPECTED EDGE per proposal, not on asset class. This is already structurally true since proposals are dispatched to the same committee regardless of type.

COMMON EDGE METRIC (per-trip risk-adjusted return, PTRAR): Define a single instrument-agnostic metric for edge comparison:
  Stock: PTRAR = realized_pnl / (entry_price * abs_position_size_usd) = return_pct_of_committed_capital
  Options multi-leg: PTRAR = realized_pnl / max_loss (where max_loss is the defined-risk amount from MultiLegProposal.max_loss, ADR-0029 D5)
Both normalize to 'how much did we make per dollar of capital at risk'. An options trade returning +2% of max_loss and a stock trade returning +2% of position have identical PTRAR and identical weight in the edge statistics pool. This eliminates a priori privileging of either class.

PTRAR_sharpe: mean(PTRAR_per_trip) / std(PTRAR_per_trip) * sqrt(annual_frequency). This is the COMMON Sharpe to report alongside the daily-returns Sharpe. It is more interpretable for comparing stock vs options outcomes.

DIFFERENTIATION in downstream agents (RISK + DELIBERATION, not DECIDE):
1. Risk agent applies DIFFERENT uncertainty adjustments: options proposals carry expiry risk (gamma spike at T-1), paper-vs-live divergence on NTA timing, and BPR uncertainty. The risk agent weights these additional uncertainties into a confidence penalty before passing to the committee. The committee then votes on the penalized signal.
2. Deliberation agent applies options-specific criteria: defined-risk requirement (max_loss must be finite, per ADR-0027), net-delta cap, BPR budget constraint. These are BLOCKING gates in the risk agent, not preference weights.
3. SILENCE asymmetry: the LLM committee may silence EITHER type of play (evidence-only role). It may NOT pick between a stock and an equivalent options play -- that is the deterministic selection table (ADR-0082).

PRACTICAL GATE: Options plays are not submitted to DECIDE until GATE-2 is passed (N>=50 round trips of stock outcomes first). Before GATE-2, options proposals are generated but held in a dry-run queue, not surfaced to the committee. After GATE-2, options plays enter the same committee queue as stock plays with no a priori order or weight advantage.

WHY THIS DESIGN: The risk is that options (especially premium-selling) show higher apparent Sharpe in paper (theta decay creates smooth daily PnL that flatters the Sharpe numerator vs stock which shows higher daily volatility). The PTRAR_sharpe metric corrects for this because both are normalized to committed capital. Any remaining difference is REAL alpha, not an artifact of the Sharpe denominator.
heuristic.reset_design:
CLEAN WINDOW START DEFINITION: A window is clean and the clock starts ONLY when ALL of: (1) quant-reset-paper-book --apply has completed (verified by state.db showing paper-default cash=100000, positions empty, executions.jsonl archived); (2) the four protective flags are set in the armed cron wrapper (DURABLE_DRAWDOWN_BASELINE=1, PER_POSITION_STOP=1, DELTA_NORMALIZER=1, ACCOUNT_LOCK=1); (3) HERMES_QUANT_PAPER_SLIPPAGE_MODEL=v0.2 is confirmed active; (4) the first autonomous tick has completed successfully without errors (proving the armed config is valid). The reset_timestamp is written to a durable file (e.g., ~/.hermes/quant/clean_window_start.json with reset_id, timestamp, nav_at_reset, flags_armed) that the evaluation/validation.py uses as t0. Any metric computed with data BEFORE this timestamp is excluded.

TOOL USAGE: Use the existing ops/scripts/quant-reset-paper-book.py --apply --yes. Deploy it first: cp ops/scripts/quant-reset-paper-book.py ~/.hermes/scripts/ (per the operator action packet step 0). The tool is idempotent (running it twice produces the same clean state), uses BEGIN IMMEDIATE atomic SQLite transaction, and backs up state.db/executions.jsonl before mutating. The backup files (*.bak-RESET-<UTC>) serve as the audit trail proving when the reset occurred.

WHEN A WINDOW IS NOT CLEAN ENOUGH TO START COUNTING: A window is NOT clean if (a) any flag was armed mid-window (the window must restart from the flag-arming moment with a fresh reset), (b) the book had a manual trade override mid-window, (c) the slippage model was changed mid-window, or (d) any universe/watchlist parameters were changed mid-window after seeing the window's results (this is the forward-contamination/peeking trap). If any of these occur, run quant-reset-paper-book --apply again and restart the clock.

POST-RESET ARMED-RAILS CHECK (pre-count condition): After reset, verify by observing the first 3-5 autonomous ticks: drawdown_pct should be non-zero if any position is opened and underwater (confirming DURABLE_DRAWDOWN_BASELINE is working); the per_position_stop_fired audit event should appear in governance audit log when a position exceeds -8% (confirming PER_POSITION_STOP is working). Only after this liveness verification does the 'clean window' officially begin counting toward GATE metrics.

SLIPPAGE HAIRCUT REQUIREMENT: HERMES_QUANT_PAPER_SLIPPAGE_MODEL=v0.2 must be on before the clock starts. Without the slippage haircut, paper Sharpe is inflated relative to live (no adverse fills, no market impact). The ADR-0097 slippage model applies a haircut to make paper fills more realistic. Running a clean window WITHOUT the slippage model and then applying it at live promotion is a bait-and-switch on the CI calculation.
heuristic.adversarial:
TRAP 1 -- Peeking / sequential significance: The most dangerous multiple-comparisons trap for AEGIS is not trying N strategies; it is WATCHING THE WINDOW and stopping early when metrics look good (or resetting when they look bad). Each 'look' at the metrics and decision to continue-or-reset is a hypothesis test. If the operator checks daily and resets on 5 consecutive losses, the effective N_strategies in the DSR formula is not 1 but O(total_trades_across_resets). This inflates the expected maximum Sharpe under the null and the DSR-adjusted threshold rises accordingly. MITIGATION: commit to a window duration in advance (minimum 60 calendar days), do NOT allow mid-window resets based on metric inspection. The quant-reset-paper-book tool should require a human-typed confirmation that includes the reason for reset; automated resets on metric thresholds are prohibited.

TRAP 2 -- Thin-sample optimism on point-estimate Sharpe: At N=50 round trips, the Lo 2002 approximation gives SE(ann_SR) ~ 1.1 at 120 trips/year. This means a point estimate of ann_SR=1.5 has a TRUE 95% CI of roughly [-0.7, +3.7]. Any single clean window that shows ann_SR=1.5 at N=50 is STATISTICALLY INDISTINGUISHABLE from SR=0 (zero edge). GATE-2 uses point-estimate thresholds ONLY because CI requirements are impractical at N=50 -- but this means GATE-2 unlocks are PROVISIONAL and must be confirmed by GATE-3 before any live consideration. Labeling GATE-2 metrics as 'preliminary' in the weekly retro output is mandatory to prevent anchoring on thin-sample numbers.

TRAP 3 -- PF gaming via W:L ratio manipulation: Profit factor = gross_wins/gross_losses. A strategy that takes tiny winners and huge losers masked by occasional big wins can show PF > 1.3 at N=50 with a convex return distribution that crashes on the 51st trade. MITIGATION: require BOTH profit_factor >= 1.3 AND max_consecutive_losses <= 8 AND max_single_loss_pct <= 10% (the per-position stop enforces the last condition). Report the W:L ratio and skewness of trade PnL in the weekly retro output alongside PF.

TRAP 4 -- Options premium-selling Sharpe inflation: A short-put strategy generates high daily SR in paper (smooth theta decay) until a gap-down assigns the position at a large loss. On a 50-trade paper window that never hits a tail event, the measured Sharpe is wildly optimistic. MITIGATION: (a) require the PTRAR_sharpe metric (normalized to max_loss, not daily returns) for options trades -- this captures the asymmetric risk correctly, (b) require the DSR calculation with kurtosis estimated from the paper return distribution (large excess kurtosis signals undiscovered tail risk), (c) never originate naked shorts (ADR-0027 defined-risk requirement already enforces this).

TRAP 5 -- Regime overfitting in a single-regime clean window: If the clean window happens to run entirely in a bull regime, the measured edge is regime-conditional, not unconditional. A strategy with edge in bull but no edge in bear will still pass all gates if the window is regime-homogeneous. MITIGATION: Report HMM regime distribution in the weekly retro for the clean window (what fraction of the window was bull/bear/neutral). Flag if > 80% of window was a single regime. Do NOT block on this, but annotate the gate-pass with regime_coverage_caveat=True.

TRAP 6 -- Correlation between the clean window and the IS parameter-fit period: The strategy parameters (recipe weights, thresholds) were tuned on historical data that may overlap with the current paper period's market regime. This is NOT a forward-test contamination in the strict lookahead sense but IS a residual IS bias. MITIGATION: treat the effective n_trials in DSR as 2+ (not 1) to add a modest multiple-comparison penalty even on the forward window, acknowledging residual IS optimization. Specifically: set n_trials=3 in the dsr.deflated_sharpe call for the gate computation, not n_trials=1.
sources: Bailey, D. and Lopez de Prado, M. (2014). 'The Deflated Sharpe Ratio: Correcting for Selection Bias, Backtest Overfitting, and Non-Normality.' Journal of Portfolio Management, 40(5), 94-107. DOI: 10.3905/jpm.2014.40.5.094. The primary academic source for DSR/PSR formulas, multiple-comparisons adjustment, and expected-maximum-Sharpe-order-statistic calculation. AEGIS already implements this in hermes_quant/evaluation/dsr.py (n_trials=1 by default for forward-only single strategy; set n_trials=3 for residual IS bias caution).

Lo, Andrew W. (2002). 'The Statistics of Sharpe Ratios.' Financial Analysts Journal, 58(4), 36-52. Establishes the asymptotic SE formula SE(SR) = sqrt((1 + 0.5*SR^2) / T) and shows that for non-iid returns the formula is a lower bound on true uncertainty. Key finding: at T=100 daily returns and ann_SR=1.5, iid SE(ann_SR) ~ 0.92, giving 95% CI lower bound of -0.30 -- confirming that N=100 round trips is NOT sufficient for SR significance under Lo formula. Block bootstrap (AEGIS's actual implementation) is tighter for autocorrelated returns.

Politis, D. and Romano, J. (1994). 'The Stationary Bootstrap.' Journal of the American Statistical Association, 89(428), 1303-1313. Politis, D. and White, H. (2004). 'Automatic Block-Length Selection for the Dependent Bootstrap.' Econometric Reviews 23(1), 53-70. Patton, A., Politis, D. and White, H. (2009). Correction note. Econometric Reviews 28(4), 372-375. These three papers define the stationary block bootstrap with automatic block-length selection that AEGIS implements in evaluation/validation.py as the PRIMARY CI method. More appropriate than BCa for autocorrelated trading returns.

Pham, T.A., Nguyen, B.C., Nguyen, T. (2026). 'AlgoXpert Alpha Research Framework: A Rigorous IS WFA OOS Protocol for Mitigating Overfitting in Quantitative Strategies.' arXiv:2603.09219 [q-fin.PM]. Confirms: (1) cliff veto / catastrophic veto rules are necessary for multi-stage OOS validation; (2) strategy rank-reversal between Sharpe-maximizing and drawdown-minimizing objectives justifies using BOTH metrics in GATE-2/GATE-3; (3) parameter lock with no further tuning during the OOS period is mandatory.

Koshiyama, A. and Firoozye, N. (2019). 'Avoiding Backtesting Overfitting by Covariance-Penalties.' arXiv:1905.05023 [q-fin.PM]. Three overfitting families identified: Data Snooping, Overestimated Performance, Cross-Validation Evaluation. Covariance-penalty correction lowers SR estimate proportional to strategy parameter count. Relevant for AEGIS: each recipe parameter is effectively a strategy choice; more complex recipes require larger N to achieve same effective evidence.

Gort, B.J.D. et al. (2022). 'Deep Reinforcement Learning for Cryptocurrency Trading: Practical Approach to Address Backtest Overfitting.' arXiv:2209.05559. Formalizes overfitting detection as hypothesis test; less-overfitted agents show higher OOS return. Confirms that the probability of overfitting metric (equivalent to Bailey-LdP PBO) is empirically predictive of forward performance.

Miller, E. (2010). 'How Not To Run an A/B Test.' evanmiller.org. Classic explanation of repeated significance testing errors (peeking trap). Directly applicable to GATE inspection pattern: checking metrics at N=20, N=30, N=40... and stopping at the first pass inflates false positive rate from 5% to ~26% by N=5 peeks. The fix is committing to N in advance (AEGIS: commit to minimum 60 calendar days, no mid-window resets on metric inspection).

synthesis.design_directive:
The AEGIS Decide+Risk design unifies four research outputs into a single coherent architecture governed by four non-negotiable posture constraints: silence-by-default, fail-CLOSED, deterministic gate is final authority, and LLM committee is evidence-only (may silence, never amplify or pick legs).

ADMISSIBLE STRUCTURES AND THE LADDER. The no-naked-leverage constraint reduces the 25-variant taxonomy to 15 admissible structures split across two buckets. Group 1 (defined-risk): Long Call, Long Put, Long Straddle, Long Strangle, Bull Call Spread, Bear Put Spread, Bull Put Spread, Bear Call Spread, Iron Condor, Iron Butterfly, Long Butterfly, Diagonal/PMCC, Protective Put, Collar, Back Spread, Stock Replacement. Group 2 (collateral-secured): Covered Call, CSP, Wheel, Covered Strangle (only when both legs independently clear). Permanently excluded: naked short call, naked short put, short straddle, short strangle, ratio spread naked portion, box spread. The discrete NAV-fraction ladder {0, +/-0.05, +/-0.10, +/-0.15, +/-0.20} maps to contract count via floor(target_nav_fraction x NAV / collateral_per_contract); collateral_per_contract is strike x 100 for CSP, basis_per_share x 100 for CC, spread_width x 100 for verticals/condors, and net_debit for PMCC/diagonals. Spreads are MORE granular on the ladder than share-backed structures because their BPR is lower. Any target that floors to zero contracts is silenced (identical to fractional equity rounding to zero). The 0.05 step is the minimum tranche unit; no fractional ladder positions are created to enable prettier tranche ratios.

TP/SL AT THE COMPOSITE VS LEG LEVEL. The 2-level model (Level-1 composite audit rollup, Level-2 position-moving legs) determines where each exit rule fires. Hard stops and take-profit logic operate at COMPOSITE level for options multi-leg structures: the 50%-of-credit TP, 2x-credit loss cap, 21-DTE close, and delta-breach close all act on the net composite P&L and net composite greeks (refreshed each tick from live leg prices via aggregate_net_greeks, never from the stale parent snapshot). The composite-level TP and loss cap fire as atomic close signals that submit a buy_to_close/sell_to_close mleg order for all legs simultaneously. For equity tranching, exits operate at the LEG level via the PortfolioState FIFO fold: each tranche step reduces the position by one 0.05 ladder rung, submitted as a single-leg equity close. The trailing stop (chandelier ATR) applies to the RESIDUAL tranche only (the half-position left after Tranche-1 TP fires) so that a noise-driven whipsaw on a small residual is a bounded loss, not a full-position liquidation. For options, the DTE-triggered close (21 DTE) is a TIME-BASED trailing mechanism at composite level: it forces composite close when remaining theta is insufficient to compensate gamma, exactly as the Huang et al. 2025 optimal-tau [50-75% of duration] result supports. The delta-breach threshold tightens inside 21 DTE (from 0.40 to 0.30 on short deltas) as a DTE-correlated composite-level monitor. For defined-risk structures, max_loss is always finite at entry (the structure IS the hard stop structurally); the 2x-credit soft stop fires before the structural maximum and is wired as a HARD RULE per the fail-CLOSED posture. The composite_plays table caches current_delta/gamma/theta/vega for hot-path monitoring; the PortfolioState fold independently tracks per-leg FIFO positions for cash/NAV/kill-switch accounting. These two levels are NEVER summed for greek aggregation (H5 hazard): composite_plays owns greek monitoring; PortfolioState owns position/cash/P&L.

STOCK-VS-OPTIONS PARITY IN DECIDE. The PDR deliberative committee (ADR-0023) treats stock Proposals and MultiLegProposals on equal footing via a single instrument-agnostic edge metric: PTRAR (per-trip risk-adjusted return) = realized_pnl / committed_capital_at_risk, where committed_capital_at_risk = entry_price x abs_position_size_usd for equity and max_loss (finite, from MultiLegProposal) for defined-risk options. A stock trade returning +2% of position and an options trade returning +2% of max_loss have identical PTRAR and identical weight in the edge statistics pool. This eliminates a priori privileging of either class. PTRAR_sharpe = mean(PTRAR_per_trip) / std(PTRAR_per_trip) x sqrt(annual_frequency) is the COMMON Sharpe reported alongside the daily-returns Sharpe. Differentiation happens DOWNSTREAM in the risk agent and deliberation agent, not in DECIDE: the risk agent applies options-specific uncertainty penalties (expiry/gamma risk, BPR uncertainty, paper-vs-live NTA timing); the deliberation agent enforces blocking gates (max_loss must be finite per ADR-0027, net-delta cap, BPR budget). The LLM committee may silence either type but may NEVER pick between a stock and an equivalent options play — that is the deterministic structure_select table (ADR-0082). Options proposals are held in a dry-run queue and NOT surfaced to the committee until GATE-2 clears (N >= 50 equity round trips AND >= 60 calendar days post-GATE-0 reset). After GATE-2, options enter the same committee queue with no order or weight advantage.

CLEAN-WINDOW GATE HIERARCHY GOVERNS THE UNLOCK SEQUENCE. GATE-0 is the prerequisite: quant-reset-paper-book --apply flattens to $100k, four protective flags armed in cron wrapper (DURABLE_DRAWDOWN_BASELINE=1, PER_POSITION_STOP=1, DELTA_NORMALIZER=1, ACCOUNT_LOCK=1), HERMES_QUANT_PAPER_SLIPPAGE_MODEL=v0.2 confirmed active, liveness verified on first 3-5 autonomous ticks. The reset_timestamp is the t0 anchor written to ~/.hermes/quant/clean_window_start.json; all metrics before t0 are poisoned and excluded. GATE-1 (N >= 20, 2-4 weeks): survival gate only — win_rate >= 0.40 Wilson-CI lower clears zero, no kill-switch fires, rolling_30d_max_drawdown <= 8%. Failure triggers strategy review, NOT live consideration. GATE-2 (N >= 50 AND >= 60 calendar days): preliminary edge gate — profit_factor_point >= 1.3, win_rate >= 0.50, rolling_90d_sharpe_point >= 0.8, max_consecutive_losses <= 8, rolling_30d_max_drawdown <= 3%, zero immutable-rule breaches. Unlocks options HITL-paper origination (proposals + human approval only, per ADR-0029 D6). CI is intentionally omitted at GATE-2 because N=50 gives CI width ~+/-3.7 under Lo 2002 — point-estimate only, labeled provisional. GATE-3 (N >= 100, existing live.py): bootstrap sharpe_95ci_lower >= 1.0, rolling_30d_max_drawdown <= 1%, no kill-switch in 14d, zero immutable breaches in 30d, calibrator_drift <= 5%. These values are hardcoded in LIVE_APPROVAL_THRESHOLDS and the LiveTradingApproval Pydantic model — do NOT change them. Options-specific live requires additionally N_options >= 100 settled multi-leg outcomes counted separately. DSR uses n_trials=3 (not 1) to apply a modest multiple-comparison penalty for residual IS bias even on the forward window. The peeking trap is mitigated by committing to the 60-calendar-day minimum window in advance; mid-window resets based on metric inspection are prohibited and require a human-typed reason if operator-forced.

BUILD ORDER is strictly sequenced by dependency gates. Step 0 (operator-only, no code): execute GATE-0 reset protocol. Step 1 (in-flight, no options code changes): complete equity foundation AG-EQ-1/2/3 plus slippage gate aegis-sl01; this starts the clean-window clock and begins accumulating GATE-1/2/3 evidence. Step 2 (after Step 1 merges, first options producer extension): Bull Put Spread recipe — add to structure_select _STRUCTURE_TABLE for (BULLISH/NEUTRAL, DEFINED_RISK_CREDIT, MID/HIGH IV) -> bull_put_spread; add StrategyKind enum value; add credit_vertical recipe; add _max_loss = (spread_width - credit) x 100 to gate classifier; gate collateral = spread_width x 100 x contracts. Step 3 (after Step 2): Bear Call Spread — mirrors Step 2 on the call side; enables both wings required for Iron Condor. Step 4 (after ADR-0029 OQ1 broker probe confirms multi-expiry mleg support): PMCC — wire shadow-to-live promotion path for the existing pmcc.py shadow tracker; add StrategyKind.pmcc to recipes; add recipe BUY LEAPS + SELL near-term OTM call; gate max_loss = net_debit. Step 5 (after Steps 2 and 3, and after GATE-2 clears): Iron Condor — compose bull_put_spread + bear_call_spread into a 4-leg structure; add StrategyKind.iron_condor; update _STRUCTURE_TABLE for (NEUTRAL, DEFINED_RISK_CREDIT, HIGH IV) -> iron_condor; this is the admissible wrapper for the highest-IR structure in the Wysocki & Slepaczuk 2024 short-strangle result (IR*** 64.2). Step 6 (after GATE-2, concurrent with Step 5): Collar — 3-leg structure using existing CC + CSP leg builders; add StrategyKind.collar; gate validates shares held + put defined-risk + call covered by shares. Step 7 (after GATE-2 and iron_condor infrastructure proven): Iron Butterfly — reuse Step 5 4-leg machinery with ATM body-strike constraint. Step 8 (deferred until GATE-3 options evidence window N_options >= 100 AND catalyst-detection integrated in Perception): Long Straddle/Strangle — requires new LONG_PREMIUM StructureIntent, low-IV-regime trigger logic, earnings-date-aware catalyst feed; defer until the income strategies have a proven paper track record and the Perception layer can feed IV-rank + binary-event signals reliably. composite_plays table (NEW, Step 2 prerequisite): CREATE TABLE in state.db with schema from the MULTILEG data model sketch; must exist before any multi-leg structure beyond CC/CSP/Wheel enters production because the DECOMPOSE/CONVERT/RAR rules and H1-H6 hazard mitigations all require it. The hazard mitigations H2 (double-count), H3 (settlement-loop parent skip), H4 (convert atomicity with 'converting' intermediate state), H5 (greek double-netting prevention), and H6 (open-composite gate before new composite on same underlying+strategy_kind) must be wired before any multi-leg structure enters HITL-paper.

synthesis.tpsl_x_multileg: At COMPOSITE level (options multi-leg structures): (1) 50%-of-credit TP — close full structure atomically when net composite MtM P&L >= 50% of initial credit; fires as a single buy_to_close/sell_to_close mleg order; supported by Huang et al. 2025 optimal-tau and tastylive practitioner evidence; EVAL-GATE-PENDING on AEGIS data. (2) 21-DTE time-triggered close — composite-level calendar rule; force-close at 21 DTE for positions opened at 40-45 DTE regardless of P&L; consistent with Huang et al. 2025 [50-75%] of duration result; tighten delta-breach threshold inside 21 DTE from 0.40 to 0.30 on short deltas. (3) 2x-credit loss cap — HARD RULE per fail-CLOSED posture; close composite when net loss >= 2x initial credit regardless of DTE or delta; fires before structural max-loss wings; wired as autonomous (not operator-gated). (4) Delta-breach close — close composite when any short delta magnitude exceeds 0.40 (pre-21 DTE) or 0.30 (inside 21 DTE); EVAL-GATE-PENDING. (5) Extrinsic-value floor for assignment prevention — close any short leg where extrinsic value <= $0.10 or 5% of original credit; wired as autonomous. Greeks refreshed each tick from live leg prices via aggregate_net_greeks(), never from stale parent snapshot in composite_plays (cached values are monitoring shorthand only; exit decisions use fresh greeks). At LEG level (equity tranching on NAV-fraction ladder): tranche exits reduce position by exactly one 0.05 ladder rung (never fractional). Full position = 0.10 NAV: Tranche-1 exits 0.05 at +1R unrealized; moves hard stop to breakeven on residual 0.05. Tranche-2 exits residual 0.05 at +2R OR when chandelier ATR trailing stop fires (whichever comes first). Trailing stop activates only after +3% unrealized gain (Li et al. 2026 top-5 configs); trailing distance 5-7% full position, 3-5% residual; ATR multiplier N=2.5x ATR(14 bars, 30-min) starting point. Stale close: 48 bars (24 hours at 30-min cadence) if no trigger fires (Li et al. 2026 directional evidence). The trailing stop NEVER promotes the position size up the ladder; it only controls WHEN to close a rung. For composite DECOMPOSE under CONVERT Rule C1 (roll): old composite transitions to 'converting' state before close-leg writes begin; new composite multi_leg_id is written to composite_plays only after all new-leg opens are written to the bus atomically inside a single append_locked call; a crash in the middle leaves the composite in 'converting' for operator review (never 'open' and never auto-resolved). All GATE-2/3 options-specific thresholds (50% TP, 21 DTE, 2x cap, delta-breach) are DEFAULT-OFF until 60-day / N>=100 options evidence window is met per ADR-0029 D7.
synthesis.stock_options_parity: Common edge metric = PTRAR (per-trip risk-adjusted return): realized_pnl / committed_capital_at_risk, where committed_capital_at_risk = entry_price x abs_position_size_usd for equity and max_loss (finite, from MultiLegProposal.max_loss per ADR-0029 D5) for defined-risk options. Both normalize to return-per-dollar-of-capital-at-risk; an equity trade returning +2% of position and an options trade returning +2% of max_loss have identical PTRAR and identical committee weight. PTRAR_sharpe = mean(PTRAR_per_trip) / std(PTRAR_per_trip) x sqrt(annual_frequency) is the COMMON Sharpe across both classes. Risk/deliberation differentiates by applying penalties AFTER PTRAR is computed: the risk agent applies options-specific uncertainty adjustments (expiry/gamma risk, BPR uncertainty, NTA timing divergence) as confidence penalties before the committee votes; the deliberation agent enforces blocking gates (finite max_loss requirement per ADR-0027, net-delta cap, BPR budget). These are BLOCKING gates applied DOWNSTREAM of DECIDE, not preference weights in the committee vote. The silence asymmetry is preserved: LLM committee may silence either class but may NEVER pick between a stock play and an equivalent options play — that selection is owned by the deterministic structure_select table. Options proposals are held in a dry-run queue and not surfaced to the committee until GATE-2 clears; after GATE-2 they enter the same committee queue with no a priori order or weight advantage. The PTRAR metric also corrects for premium-selling Sharpe inflation (smooth theta decay flatters daily-return Sharpe vs equity): because both are normalized to committed capital, any remaining measured PTRAR_sharpe difference between equity and options is real alpha, not a denominator artifact.
